issue.title: UMBRELLA: Computational Atomic Physics — Theoretical Codex transition-data initiative
issue.description:
## Mission

Establish an independent, reproducible computational atomic-physics workstream producing critically assessed theoretical transition data for UV/VIS/IR abundance analysis, beginning with O I/O II as applicable and Fe I/II. This is NOT permission to relabel theoretical predictions as laboratory measurements or publish unvalidated abundances.

## Mandatory preflight

Read current GitHub Project Register, Target Star List, Canonical Element List, SCIENCE_STANDARDS, docs/ELEMENT_PROTOCOL.md and current canonical_gf/line-grade schemas; review full Linear <issue id="f1039187-38b1-463a-98eb-ed3b4e9e7c5e" label="RYA-946" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-946/umbrella-all-element-laboratory-gf-sweep-literature-validation" /> (including comments), <issue id="ba14af3e-7806-4c30-a118-5a0cc43999a9" label="RYA-1169" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-1169/si-build-gf-graded-line-sets-agss21-reference-census-asplund-codex" />, <issue id="be8bf507-78b1-4ec2-a238-f33af47d19cf" label="RYA-709" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-709/umbrella-the-26-element-sweep-every-element-gets-the-protocol-10852" />, <issue id="8eb95d16-a86e-4de7-86f4-b17df02b1cab" label="RYA-587" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-587/architecture-27-element-reported-uncertainty-generalization-rya-282-5" />, <issue id="68caa0a1-dd50-4c03-8386-a6c7ab48d24b" label="RYA-161" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-161/science-solar-astrophysical-log-gf-calibration-blue-edge-cut" />, <issue id="49d10ad1-6867-4ac1-86b8-031b6001329c" label="RYA-945" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-945/ingest-fe-iii-laboratory-gf-into-canonical-gf-obriannist-c-den-hartog" />, <issue id="a93ba5bf-5b56-42fe-9610-56e51df57d19" label="RYA-822" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-822/build-extend-adjudicate-canonical-gf-blueward-of-3780-a-the-near-uv-fe" />, <issue id="c51601ef-a026-4a70-a542-96d4cb42e331" label="RYA-1131" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-1131/intake-cno-solar-reference-lines-across-fuvnuvir-agss21-lineage-plus" />, and current O/Fe Bridge work. GitHub connector discovery was incomplete at ticket creation: verify actual repository state before changing code. Identify any contradictory historical grading policy and report it.

## Scientific contract

Preserve existing Asplund, Reference, Codex (primary experimental gf, depth <=0.60), and Deep (primary experimental gf, depth >0.60) semantics. Proposed new class: THEORETICAL_CODEX; approval is conditional on governance review. Separate origin/evidence type, grade/line-selection, accuracy/uncertainty, and usability status. Never confer NIST experimental-grade status on theoretical values. Preserve independent primary experimental, NIST evaluated, VALD/Kurucz, theoretical, and astrophysical gf records without silent overwrites. A theoretical transition is a *candidate* until blind benchmarks and uncertainty review pass. No tuning to the Solar abundance.

## Deliverables

1. Reproducible all-band census of currently used, excluded, ungraded, and theoretically tractable lines, matched by species/ion, energy levels, wavelength medium/frame, and HFS/isotope component identity (never wavelength alone).
2. Atomic-property scope: observed/theoretical levels and wavelengths, f/loggf, Einstein A, lifetimes, branching fractions, selection rules, level mixing, Landé g, HFS/isotope constants where tractable, natural broadening; separately scoped Stark/van der Waals/ABO, photoionization, electron/H collision data and NLTE completeness, with method-appropriate solvers and limitations.
3. Benchmark GRASP/MCDHF against independent atomic structure method where scientifically appropriate; convergence, correlation, relativistic, gauge, observed-level substitution and uncertainty validation; blind withheld primary lab comparisons, not just internal agreement.
4. Machine-readable versioned atomic-data products with code/version/input provenance, atomic source DOI, confidence/uncertainty covariance, reproducible commands, benchmark reports and rejected candidates.
5. Integration gates with <issue id="8eb95d16-a86e-4de7-86f4-b17df02b1cab" label="RYA-587" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-587/architecture-27-element-reported-uncertainty-generalization-rya-282-5" /> uncertainty budget, <issue id="be8bf507-78b1-4ec2-a238-f33af47d19cf" label="RYA-709" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-709/umbrella-the-26-element-sweep-every-element-gets-the-protocol-10852" /> accounting, stellar line-selection, website provenance, and mandatory verified IR telluric correction.
6. O first, Fe cross-band stress test second, M-dwarf applicability assessment including molecular blends, pressure broadening and magnetism.

## Acceptance

No current line grade silently changes; no existing published abundance is altered; all additions opt-in behind explicit scientific review. Maintain critical/warning/suggestion audit and create PRs for review, not direct publication.

issue.title: UMBRELLA: all-element laboratory-gf sweep + literature validation (replicate the line list, not the model) — canonical elements beyond Fe
issue.description:
## Goal

Sweep the <issue id="49d10ad1-6867-4ac1-86b8-031b6001329c" label="RYA-945" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-945/ingest-fe-iii-laboratory-gf-into-canonical-gf-obriannist-c-den-hartog" /> Fe lab-gf template across every canonical element. For each element: ingest the definitive laboratory-gf line list, collect the published literature abundance values, run our full multi-engine x multi-atlas matrix on the FIXED line list, and produce an error plot — literature consensus band vs our per-engine results.

## Governing method (ratified this session — applies to every child)

The validation is NOT reproduction of a reference study's model atmosphere or code. "Replicate the experiment" means replicate the **line list**, not the 1974 model. Precisely:

* **Fixed asset:** the atomic line list (wavelengths + lab/graded gf) is established ONCE per element from the reference lab studies, and is shared across all engines AND all target stars. It does not change between engines or between stars. This is why it must be right — every Codex target inherits it.
* **Variable:** the engine (route . scale . model . atmos . code) and the atlas/instrument. We run the fixed lines through the full matrix (EW/synth x 1D-LTE/1D-NLTE/3D-NLTE x MARCS x Bergemann/Amarsi/Gerber x Kurucz-flux / Delbouille-intensity / HARPS / CRIRES+).
* **Reference comparison isolates the engine:** hold what the reference study held — same lines, same gf, same spectrum — and the ONLY difference is our engine vs theirs. We do NOT match their model atmosphere or code. Their published value is "what they got with their setup," a point on the plot.
* **The deliverable is an error plot**, not a bit-match: published literature values with their error bars (Lodders meteoritic; Asplund/AAG photospheric; the element's lab-study solar values e.g. Den Hartog/Ruffoni; Scott 2015; Caffau; Bergemann) = the consensus band. Overlay OUR per-engine results on the same fixed lines. Question: given the same lines and gf, what does our engine get, and does it land in the band?
* Validate-don't-tune (<issue id="68caa0a1-dd50-4c03-8386-a6c7ab48d24b" label="RYA-161" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-161/science-solar-astrophysical-log-gf-calibration-blue-edge-cut" />) holds: nothing tuned to match; each engine reports what the fixed lines give. Agreement validates line list + engine; the engine-to-engine and engine-vs-literature spread IS the systematic meter, not error to hide.

## Per-element child structure

### Mandatory uncertainty inheritance (2026-09-15)

Every element child inherits <issue id="8eb95d16-a86e-4de7-86f4-b17df02b1cab" label="RYA-587" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-587/architecture-27-element-reported-uncertainty-generalization-rya-282-5" /> as the single canonical uncertainty protocol. This includes product-specific statistical/fit uncertainty, atomic/molecular-data uncertainty, stellar-parameter perturbations, ξ where physically applicable, observation/reduction terms, model/physics terms, covariance, and matched Solar/reference differential uncertainty before target-star publication. A child that merely reports `sigma_stat`/gf/ξ without the applicable <issue id="8eb95d16-a86e-4de7-86f4-b17df02b1cab" label="RYA-587" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-587/architecture-27-element-reported-uncertainty-generalization-rya-282-5" /> stack is incomplete. Do not fork/rewrite the recipe locally; reference and execute the canonical implementation.

One child ticket per element (Mr. Code brief, <issue id="49d10ad1-6867-4ac1-86b8-031b6001329c" label="RYA-945" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-945/ingest-fe-iii-laboratory-gf-into-canonical-gf-obriannist-c-den-hartog" /> pattern). Each child:

1. Ingest the definitive lab-gf sources into `canonical_gf` (crossmatch-verified; precedence lab > NIST-C+ > Kurucz > VALD; EP cut where the literature applies one).
2. Collect the literature abundance values (litscan band, <issue id="63bfeeb4-1363-4208-ac3f-83e5f5f52d54" label="RYA-714" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-714/litscan-findings-fe-i-solar-photospheric-uvvisir-audit" /> pattern) with verified citations.
3. Run the multi-engine x multi-atlas matrix on the fixed lines.
4. Produce the error plot: literature band + our per-engine results.

**Every source verified against ADS/VizieR per child — NO fabricated citations (the** <issue id="49d10ad1-6867-4ac1-86b8-031b6001329c" label="RYA-945" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-945/ingest-fe-iii-laboratory-gf-into-canonical-gf-obriannist-c-den-hartog" /> **discipline, learned the hard way this session).**

## Lab-gf source map (POINTERS ONLY — each child verifies exact ref + VizieR ID + DOI before ingesting)

* **Fe I/II** — O'Brian 1991 / Den Hartog 2014 / Ruffoni 2014 / Belmonte 2017 / Den Hartog 2019 — DONE, <issue id="49d10ad1-6867-4ac1-86b8-031b6001329c" label="RYA-945" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-945/ingest-fe-iii-laboratory-gf-into-canonical-gf-obriannist-c-den-hartog" /> (the template)
* **Ti I / Ti II** — Lawler+2013 / Wood+2013 (Wisconsin)
* **V I / V II** — Lawler+2014 / Wood+2014
* **Cr I / Cr II** — Sobeck, Lawler & Sneden 2007 / Cr II lab
* **Mn I/II** — Den Hartog / Blackwell-Whitehead & Bergemann 2007
* **Ni I** — Wood+2014
* **Co I, Sc II** — Lawler group
* **Alphas (Mg, Si, Ca)** — element-specific lab studies (e.g. Mg: Pehlivan Rhodin+) + NIST-C+
* **C, N, O** — high-excitation atomic + molecular (Amarsi 2021 3D-LTE molecular for solar CNO); NLTE-sensitive, treat carefully
* **Neutron-capture (Ba, Sr, Y, Zr, Eu)** — Lawler group r/s-process transition-probability papers
* **Na, Al, K, P, Cu, Li** — NIST-C+ + dedicated per-element lab studies

Each entry is a POINTER, not a citation. The child ticket pins the exact reference, VizieR catalogue, and DOI, and verifies before ingesting.

## Priority sequencing (science-first, not alphabetical)

1. **Fe** — <issue id="49d10ad1-6867-4ac1-86b8-031b6001329c" label="RYA-945" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-945/ingest-fe-iii-laboratory-gf-into-canonical-gf-obriannist-c-den-hartog" /> (template, in progress)
2. **C, N, O** — flagship C/O ratio (the Codex's headline science)
3. **CHNOPS + alphas** (Mg, Si, Ca, S, Ti) — habitability set
4. **Fe-peak** (Cr, Mn, Co, Ni, V, Sc, Cu)
5. **Neutron-capture** (Ba, Sr, Y, Zr, Eu) + Na, Al, K, P, Li

This lands the Sun's flagship deliverables (C/O, CHNOPS) first; Alpha Cen and 55 Cnc inherit the validated lists.

## Gate

Children open AFTER <issue id="49d10ad1-6867-4ac1-86b8-031b6001329c" label="RYA-945" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-945/ingest-fe-iii-laboratory-gf-into-canonical-gf-obriannist-c-den-hartog" /> validates the template — i.e., Fe lands in the literature band on the Den Hartog 2014 flux reproduction (7.45 on the Kurucz flux atlas). If the crossmatch / precedence / HFS machinery needs fixing, fix it on Fe ONCE, then clone. One validated template beats 27 speculative tickets.

## Reconcile

<issue id="4096f5f6-0ee8-4046-b45a-a79601ac6f1e" label="RYA-752" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-752/umbrella-systematic-gf-scale-audit-codex-kitt-peak-chain-nssi-036-042" /> (N/S/Si gf-scale audit umbrella) and <issue id="634dcd19-0f7a-45cc-aee3-325aa65d9731" label="RYA-697" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-697/science-gf-zero-point-floor-cluster-s-i-n-i-p-i-cu-i-successor-home" /> (S/N/P/Cu zero-point cluster) predate this and are unexecuted — assess whether they are subsumed/superseded by this systematic sweep and fold in or close as part of the C/N/O and alpha children.

Related: <issue id="49d10ad1-6867-4ac1-86b8-031b6001329c" label="RYA-945" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-945/ingest-fe-iii-laboratory-gf-into-canonical-gf-obriannist-c-den-hartog" /> (Fe template), <issue id="63bfeeb4-1363-4208-ac3f-83e5f5f52d54" label="RYA-714" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-714/litscan-findings-fe-i-solar-photospheric-uvvisir-audit" /> (litscan reference bands), <issue id="68caa0a1-dd50-4c03-8386-a6c7ab48d24b" label="RYA-161" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-161/science-solar-astrophysical-log-gf-calibration-blue-edge-cut" /> (validate-don't-tune), <issue id="a93ba5bf-5b56-42fe-9610-56e51df57d19" label="RYA-822" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-822/build-extend-adjudicate-canonical-gf-blueward-of-3780-a-the-near-uv-fe" />/834 (canonical_gf machinery), <issue id="4096f5f6-0ee8-4046-b45a-a79601ac6f1e" label="RYA-752" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-752/umbrella-systematic-gf-scale-audit-codex-kitt-peak-chain-nssi-036-042" /> / <issue id="634dcd19-0f7a-45cc-aee3-325aa65d9731" label="RYA-697" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-697/science-gf-zero-point-floor-cluster-s-i-n-i-p-i-cu-i-successor-home" /> (prior gf-cluster umbrellas to reconcile).

## Mandatory Solar reference-line-set census — AGSS21 lineage, all bands (added 2026-08-29)

For **every canonical element**, before the lab-gf sweep is called complete, reconstruct the exact transition set(s) used to derive the adopted Solar photospheric value and cross-reference those rows against Codex. This is the all-element generalisation of <issue id="c0ab6b71-4ad1-4182-8796-f7a80c74b437" label="RYA-1109" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-1109/source-create-the-asplund-agss21-solar-fe-line-list-gf-the-reference" />, not merely a citation/value litscan.

### Scope

* Trace the adopted value in Asplund, Amarsi & Grevesse 2021 (AGSS21) to its actual line-level source.
* Search **all wavelength regions used by the source analysis**: FUV, NUV, VIS, red optical, NIR, and IR, including atomic, forbidden, molecular, isotopologue, and blend-component indicators where applicable.
* If AGSS21 publishes the rows directly, transcribe that table with extraction controls, as <issue id="c0ab6b71-4ad1-4182-8796-f7a80c74b437" label="RYA-1109" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-1109/source-create-the-asplund-agss21-solar-fe-line-list-gf-the-reference" /> did for Fe.
* If AGSS21 only summarizes an earlier element-specific analysis, follow its citations to the source paper/table/catalog and reconstruct the rows there. Do not label a generic canonical candidate as “Asplund-used.”
* Preserve explicit negative selections and scope statements. Example: AGSS21's Fe footnote rejects available Ruffoni IR Fe I lines as too strong/blended; that is a published selection fact, not a missing-band accident.
* Keep separate line sets when the adopted Solar value combines indicators or papers (for example atomic vs molecular, permitted vs forbidden, or UV vs optical/IR).

### Required per-line join

Each literature-used line must carry, at minimum:

`reference_line_set | adopted_solar_value_lineage | source_paper/table/catalog | species/isotopologue | wavelength + medium | EP/transition identity | published loggf | published gf source if stated | published EW/profile/weight/exclusion | source band | Codex canonical_line_id | Codex loggf | Codex gf_tier | Codex nist_grade | Codex lab source/sigma/DOI | delta_loggf | join_status | ambiguity/status note`

Crossmatch through the canonical physical-transition matcher (species/ion + wavelength/frame + EP/levels/component identity), never wavelength alone.

### Deliverables and gates

1. A machine-readable **published Solar reference line set** for every element, including excluded/quarantined rows rather than silently dropping them.
2. A per-band coverage matrix: published-used, published-explicitly-rejected, Codex-matched, Codex-graded, Codex-ungraded, missing, ambiguous.
3. A source-lineage note proving how those lines lead to the adopted AGSS21 Solar value, or an explicit `SOURCE_LINE_LIST_NOT_PUBLISHED` wall after the cited primary sources/supplements/catalogues were checked.
4. A Codex comparison separating:
   * used by AGSS21/source analysis **and** graded by Codex;
   * used there but ungraded/fallback in Codex;
   * graded in Codex but not used there;
   * absent from Codex;
   * excluded by the source analysis.
5. No element is `FROZEN_READY_FOR_MEASUREMENT` until this cross-reference is complete or a documented, approved source-publication exception exists.

“AGSS21 adopted this abundance” is not evidence that AGSS21 used every line in Codex, and an AGSS21 abundance value is not a gf grade. Never infer the line set from the final abundance or from proximity to familiar diagnostic wavelengths.

## 2026-09-13 bibliography/provenance gate — required for every element gf/reference sweep

All children of this umbrella must scan the applicable project **Reference Documents** holdings and reconcile them with the canonical bibliography while performing the line/gf/reference audit.

Requirements:

* inventory applicable local papers/tables/supplements before external searching;
* every adopted gf/atomic-data source, reference-line study, model/NLTE/3D source, molecular/indicator source, and validation paper must resolve to one canonical bibliography entry;
* new sources discovered during the sweep must add/update the bibliography in the same ticket/PR;
* deduplicate alternate citations/copies and retain authoritative DOI/ADS/bibcode or equivalent metadata where available;
* bibliography identity must remain distinct from local PDF availability — valid sources without a local copy are still cited and their document state recorded;
* no fabricated citation metadata; unresolved metadata remains explicit;
* line/gf provenance keys and later abundance/product references must resolve back to these canonical records.

**Freeze gate addition:** no element line/gf pool is `FROZEN_READY_FOR_MEASUREMENT` until its adopted scientific provenance is bibliography-resolvable and the applicable Reference Documents scan is documented.

Closeout must report: `reference_documents_scanned`, bibliography additions/updates, duplicate reconciliation, missing-local-copy sources, unresolved metadata, and provenance-key validation.

This implements the standing <issue id="be8bf507-78b1-4ec2-a238-f33af47d19cf" label="RYA-709" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-709/umbrella-the-26-element-sweep-every-element-gets-the-protocol-10852" /> Reference Documents ↔ bibliography requirement.

attachments.title: RYA-1173: the AGSS21-lineage solar Al reference line set + RYA-946 census, and the gate that enforces it

comments.body:
RATIFIED (Ryan, 2026-09-03) -- top-grade construction for lab-poor elements + its firewall. Amends the 2026-08-30 grade definitions.

POLICY. The top reference grade is built by AMALGAMATING the best available gf for each line from every source we can find -- the same construction Asplund et al. use to assemble their line set. Best lab result per line where one exists; evaluated-theoretical (Opacity Project / MCHF and the like) where no lab measurement exists. We will NOT get lab-only every time, and that is acceptable by design: the deliverable is "best available per line, sourced with inline citation," not "lab-only."

THE ONE FIREWALL (non-circular). We never adopt another analysis's SOLAR-DERIVED values -- no astrophysical/solar-fitted gf, no borrowed solar abundance. We amalgamate the INPUT gf compilations they used; we never import their OUTPUT. That is the line between replicating a line list (allowed -- the whole point) and circularity (forbidden, RYA-161).

SCOPE. This activates the evaluated tier as the honest ACTIVE headline for every element where no primary-lab tier exists above it -- resolving the CNO "too good to be nothing, not lab so not Codex, Consistent is parked" hole and generalizing to every lab-gf-less element in the roster. Labeled evaluated/amalgamated, NEVER lab: the Codex/Deep = primary-lab-only firewall (2026-08-30) stays intact. This adds a top reference tier beside the depth grid; it does NOT loosen Codex/Deep.

CONFIRMED IN PRACTICE. The pattern is already how intake runs: Al amalgamated Vujnovic + Burheim + Johnson (RYA-1132/1001); Si built the same Asplund/Codex/Deep census (RYA-1169); CNO amalgamated NIST ASD + Amarsi (RYA-1160). This ratifies what the intake already does.

NAME -- OPEN. The tier is currently called "Asplund," which reads as a person and risks implying we import his values (we do not). Candidates: Reference Grade, Consensus Grade, Benchmark Grade, Compilation Grade. Policy is ratified now; the name is to be pinned separately (Ryan's pick).

RATIFIED LINE-GRADE DEFINITIONS (Ryan, 2026-08-30). Resolves RYA-1105's open mapping + the drift Mr Code surfaced. THREE active grades, PRIMARY-LAB gf only. Two orthogonal axes -- do not conflate them (that conflation WAS the drift).

AXIS 1 -- measurement route (feature-depth / saturation; settled, correct):
AXIS 2 -- gf provenance (primary-lab only for active grades; the drift is resolved by pinning CODE as truth).

Active grades:
- CODEX GRADE (code: graded) = primary-laboratory gf, solar feature depth <= 0.60. Unsaturated, EW-valid. The adopted-abundance workhorse. Feature depth = max component depth within 0.05 A, measured from the solar spectrum.
- DEEP GRADE (code: deepgraded) = primary-laboratory gf, feature depth > 0.60. Saturated -> EW inversion breaks down -> routed to SYNTHESIS. Same lab-gf quality as Codex Grade; differs ONLY by route (the strong-line axis). NOT a lower-quality tier.
- ASPLUND GRADE (code: asplund) = ORTHOGONAL to the depth grid: the external reference line-set (AGSS21 + reference gf), the replication/validation anchor. Not part of the graded/deep-graded provenance grid.

Floor + gaps (unchanged): depth < 0.05 = below observability, reported separately; empty graded/deep-graded cells = REAL coverage gaps, never backfilled with fallback lines.

PARKED (gated, reversible -- RYA-1105):
- CONSISTENT = the EVALUATED provenance tier (NIST-C+/evaluated gf, distinct from primary-lab). A FUTURE product when processing time + a faster machine allow. Gated-not-deleted. Do NOT merge evaluated gf into Codex/Deep Grade -- provenance stays unblurred.

DRIFT RESOLUTION: code selects LAB-only; RYA-946 policy text said 'LAB or NIST-C+'. Pin the CODE as truth; the policy text is the error -> fix it to primary-LAB-only. Do not loosen the headline tier to swallow NIST-evaluated gf.

FOLLOW-ON (separate, do not block CNO): one alignment pass so code, policy text, register (RYA-1101), and the tier/line_set CSVs all state this ONE definition (single source of truth). OPEN to verify in that pass: the exact 'NIST-C+' threshold -- if it means 'C or better' it conflicts with the method doc's A+/A/B-only rule (a second drift to clean). CNO graded/deep-graded pools now unblocked against these definitions.

## Missing-band intake opened

Created **RYA-1131** and started it immediately for the missing CNO FUV/NUV/IR and molecular Solar reference assets.

It owns AGSS21/source-line tracing, acquisition, verified transcription, all-band coverage, and the physical-transition join to Codex for C I/C II, N I/N II, O I/[O I]/O II plus CH, C2, CN, NH, OH, CO and relevant isotopologues/blend components.

RYA-1130 remains the schema owner. RYA-1131 source acquisition/audit is active now; only final molecular canonicalization waits for RYA-1130.

## Wave 1 CNO intake checkpoint

PR: https://github.com/damienabraxas/exoplanetcodex/pull/477
Branch: `ryandamienschmitt/rya-1129-phase-a-intake`
Commit: `15a6d90`

### Live registry result

- authoritative `data/config/elements_master.json`: 27 target rows, **26 unique atomic symbols**
- Zn is absent from that registry despite RYA-757-era artifacts calling it the 28th canonical element
- the new ledger follows the registry and records the contradiction; it does not invent a Zn row

### C/N/O atomic findings

| element | atomic rows | primary-lab tagged | evaluated/NIST | fallback | explicit source DOI | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| C | 1,788 | 0 | 1 | 1,392 | 0 | CROSSMATCH_REVIEW |
| N | 474 | 0 | 0 | 14 | 0 | CROSSMATCH_REVIEW |
| O | 559 | 0 | 4 | 158 | 0 | CROSSMATCH_REVIEW |

Generated:
- `data/audit/rya1129_atomic_intake/{C,N,O}_atomic_manifest.csv`
- `data/audit/rya1129_atomic_intake/intake_status_ledger.csv`
- `data/audit/rya1129_atomic_intake/manifest_metadata.json`
- `docs/science/rya1129_cno_atomic_intake.md`
- reproducible builder + tests

No gf was changed and no abundance was generated or tuned.

### Mandatory schema stop

Molecular rows cannot meet the ticket's provenance contract in the current atomic schema: CH 2,265; C2 2,654; CN 2,766; NH 114; OH 1; CO 0. Existing molecular rows are effectively VALD3-labelled without row-level DOI/release/isotopologue/transition/partition-function/dissociation-energy provenance. Created **RYA-1130** for the typed molecular provenance schema and linked it as blocking RYA-1129.

### Verification

- builder reproduced all artifacts
- targeted tests: **8 passed**
- `git diff --check`: clean
- broader stewardship collection is blocked on this host's Python 3.9 by pre-existing PEP 604 syntax (`str | None`), not by this change

### Resume point

Land/review PR 477, reconcile the registry/Zn contradiction, then resolve exact row-level sources for the pipeline C I/N I/O I indicators while RYA-1130 establishes the molecular representation. C/N/O are **not** `FROZEN_READY_FOR_MEASUREMENT`.

INTAKE STAGING + TIERED-RIGOR (Ryan, 2026-08-29). Two additions to this umbrella.

## A. TIERED-RIGOR SWEEP POLICY
The sweep runs each element at its HIGHEST VALIDATED RUNG, not Fe-depth on every element (1123 Rule 5). Fe got the full ladder because it is the anchor + proving ground; that work is DONE and the recipe (uncertainty stack RYA-282, line tiers, model ladder, firewalls) is now reusable infrastructure. Per element: run the fidelity its available grids + line data support (e.g. 1D-NLTE Bergemann if that is the ceiling; do NOT build a bespoke <3D> deck an element will never need), report that rung honestly with its real uncertainty, mark missing higher rungs visibly (never zero-fill). Depth matched to what exists, not forced uniform. THIS is the speed unlock: the other elements are recipe APPLICATION, not re-derivation. NOT a rigor cut -- you report the tier you actually have, never fake a higher one (RYA-161).

## B. INTAKE RUNS AHEAD OF THE SWEEP (ungated)
This umbrella's gate ("children open after the Fe template validates") governs the SWEEP children (ingest lab-gf, run matrix, error plot). It does NOT block INTAKE. Line-list prep (VALD extraction -> verification -> build -> data audit) is MECHANICAL, recipe-fixed, and needed REGARDLESS of how the sweep lands -- so it stages + runs NOW, in parallel, for every element. When an element's sweep opens, its lines are already in hand. This is the cheap-token, ChatGPT-executable layer.

## C. PER-ELEMENT INTAKE TEMPLATE (clone per element)
Fixed recipe (skills carry it: codex-vald-extraction, codex-data-audit), element params plugged in:
1. VALD extraction -- Extract Stellar form recipe, HFS-splitting ON (mandatory), 100k truncation trap, per-element naming, solar params; element-specific diagnostic wavelength ranges (UV/VIS/IR).
2. Intake verification -- truncation / coverage / HFS / ACCEPT-REJECT gate.
3. Line-list build -- assemble + crossmatch to canonical_gf, lambda+EP dual key (RYA-1037).
4. Data audit -- codex-data-audit on the holdings covering the element's bands (product type, BERV, telluric, SNR, units, FITS).
Firewall: NO fabricated citations -- every source verified vs ADS/VizieR (the RYA-945 discipline).

## D. ROSTER (25 beyond Fe, RYA-946 priority order; HFS = HFS-on especially critical)
- CNO flagship: C, N, O (molecular bands relevant CH/CN/OH/CO; NLTE-sensitive).
- CHNOPS + alphas: Mg, Si, Ca, S, Ti.
- Fe-peak: Cr, Mn(HFS), Co(HFS), Ni, V(HFS), Sc(HFS), Cu(HFS).
- n-capture + light odd-Z: Ba(HFS/iso), Sr, Y, Zr, Eu(HFS/iso), Na(HFS), Al(HFS), K(HFS), P, Li.
(Zn pending RYA-757, 27->28.)

## E. INSTANTIATION
The per-element intake tickets are MECHANICAL CLONES of template C. Instantiate via ChatGPT / batch (Ryan: save Claude tokens) -- one intake ticket per roster element, linked to this umbrella, sweep child kept gated. Claude provides the template + roster (this comment); the cloning + execution is the cheap-token layer.

STANDING CONVENTION -- gf treatment is MANDATORY for every canonical element (Ryan, 2026-08-23). This umbrella (RYA-946) is its authoritative home; RYA-179 carries the cross-copy; element sweeps (RYA-709) and per-element umbrellas reference it, not restate it (RYA-270).

THE CONVENTION: every element runs the full gf pipeline Fe established, in order:
1. LAB-GF CENSUS -- find EVERY line with lab-grade gf available (the rya824-style sub-pool selection). Fe found 99 unused lab-gf lines this way; do not assume the swapped set is the complete available set.
2. LAB-GF SWAP -- swap to lab values with per-line sigma + citation (the Burheim/DH14/RU14/BEL17 pattern).
3. GRADED SUB-POOL -- build the graded anchor (the Fe 163-line analogue).
4. ZERO-POINT CAP -- compute the RYA-987/968 cap. This is the OFFSET DETECTOR: it is the step that reveals a gf zero-point systematic. An element without a computed cap has an UNDETECTED gf offset (this is exactly the suspected Al defect, RYA-1023).
5. PER-BAND COVERAGE -- run the treatment across ALL bands the element is measured in, not just the headline band (Fe's red-optical/NIR were the miss; check every element for the same).

BEST-EFFORT ON COVERAGE, HONEST ON THE WALL (Ryan's framing -- "fine if we can't find all the graded lines in the world, but we better try our damn best"):
- The gf treatment is a MANDATORY STEP, not optional. Every element gets it.
- Coverage is BEST-EFFORT: grade every line that HAS lab gf.
- Where lab gf genuinely does NOT exist for a line/band, that is a DOCUMENTED WALL, never a silent skip -- record it explicitly (like Fe's >11013 A NIR: ungraded by absence of laboratory measurement, honestly recorded). "Better lab gf is the only lever" is a legitimate, publishable end-state for a line -- but only once we have PROVEN the lab gf does not exist, not assumed it.
- DELIVERABLE per element: "graded what has lab gf + documented what does not," NOT "everything graded." An element is NOT DONE until its gf treatment is run and its ungraded remainder is explicitly recorded.

ANTI-TUNING FIREWALL (RYA-161, absolute): grade to get the gf RIGHT, never to hit a literature value. If correct gf happens to move an element toward Asplund/Lodders, good; but the target is the correct gf scale, never the reference band. Uniform-vs-subset per-line check (RYA-1021) distinguishes a zero-point offset from a per-line gf error.

TEMPLATE: RYA-1023 (the Al gf-treatment audit) is the worked checklist -- every element's gf treatment gets audited against those five steps. Fe (RYA-961/968/987/824) is the reference implementation.

Related: RYA-946 (this umbrella), RYA-179 (convention cross-copy), RYA-709 (26-element sweep -- references this), RYA-968/987/824/961 (the Fe reference implementation), RYA-1023 (the Al audit template), RYA-161 (anti-tuning), RYA-1021 (uniform-vs-subset), RYA-752 (the N/S/Si gf-offset umbrella -- a symptom this convention systematically addresses).

## Umbrella assessment — gate status, sweep size, and the RYA-752 / RYA-697 reconcile (2026-08-22)

Read-only assessment against `main` @ `94c380e` (RYA-945 merged). Nothing committed.

### 1. Gate status: NOT met — and RYA-951 will not satisfy it

The gate is *"Fe lands in the literature band on the Den Hartog 2014 flux reproduction (**7.45 on the Kurucz flux atlas**)."*

RYA-951 runs the graded pool on **telluric-corrected HARPS** — a different atlas, so it answers a different question. The gate needs its own graded Fe I run on the Kurucz flux holding. Decision needed: widen 951 to both atlases, or file a separate gate run.

### 2. Sweep size: lab gf exists for **Fe only**

Measured on `canonical_gf` (167,739 rows):

| | rows |
| -- | --: |
| carrying a `lab_source_tag` | **2,157** |
| — Fe I | 1,576 |
| — Fe II | 581 |
| — **every other species** | **0** |

Tags: NIST-C+ 1710, DH14 199, RU14 129, BEL17 73, DH19 22.

Everything else in the table — Cr I 10,740 · Ti I 8,124 · Ca I 6,679 · V I 6,188 · Mn I 5,285 · Co I 4,372 · Ni I 2,717 · S I 1,950 — is seeded from `synth(GES)`, `linelist(VALD3)` or `NIST` with **no lab pedigree at all**. The umbrella's scope estimate is accurate: 1 species done, ~26 elements to go.

### 3. 🔴 Fe II is not gradeable — filed as RYA-953

RYA-945 ingested 581 Fe II lab-tagged rows, but no Fe II product can be graded, so every Fe II cell still charges the ungraded 0.17.

The trap: `LAB_GRADED_SPECIES = frozenset({("Fe","I")})` **is correct today.** `gf_grades.LAB_CSV` is `fe1_lab_loggf.csv` — 465 rows, **Fe I only**. Flipping the constant would referee Fe II against Fe I lab rows on wavelength and EP alone — the exact "manufacture a graded pool out of a coincidence" failure its own docstring names. The table must exist first.

Also, of those 581 Fe II rows: **559 are NIST-C+** (an accuracy *grade*, not a measurement) and only **22 are DH19** (genuine primary lab). Median σ 0.0719 dex.

RYA-953 carries the verified FERRUM-project source map (all DOIs Crossref-resolved), including which FERRUM papers to **exclude** — Hartman 2003 and Gurell 2009 are *forbidden* [Fe II] lines, nebular diagnostics that a wavelength/EP crossmatch would happily accept into a photospheric pool.

**This generalises:** step 3 of RYA-953 is to make `gf_grades` species-keyed rather than Fe I hardcoded. Every child of this umbrella needs that, so it should land once, on Fe II, as part of the template — not 26 times.

### 4. ⚠️ The bar will not land where the children expect

`gf_rung.decide()` computes the cited term as the **RMS** of per-line sigmas, not the median. On the post-945 table:

| band | n lab lines | median σ | **RMS σ** | coverage |
| -- | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| near-UV | 89 | 0.0300 | 0.0527 | 100% |
| VIS | 225 | 0.0300 | **0.0503** | 100% |
| red-optical | 65 | 0.0300 | 0.0503 | 100% |
| IR | 42 | 0.0400 | 0.0597 | 100% |

The distribution is skewed, so a child expecting "0.03" from the median will see **~0.05**. That is still 3.3× better than the ungraded 0.17, but it sits **above** the 0.041 generic bound — rung 3 *widens* relative to the bound, exactly as `gf_rung`'s docstring warns ("Rung 3 is not 'the smaller number' — it is the MEASURED one, and it moves either way"). Worth stating in the child template so nobody reads a correct result as a regression.

### 5. Reconcile verdict: fold both in, **close neither**

**RYA-697 → re-scope as required triage step 0 of each child.** Not a duplicate — a precondition. Its whole finding is that "gf" was the *recorded* blocker for elements whose real blocker was something else: Al was saturation, Y was saturation + ion-label, and **P I's 6.610 is a railed fit** (`status='edge_pinned'`, bound = Asplund + 1.2 = 6.61 exactly). Ti was the one that genuinely was gf.

This collides directly with the showcase convention ratified above. SHOWCASE = the graded pool is *always* the reported value, with its tight cited-σ bar. Ingest good lab gf for P I without first clearing the rail, and the showcase tier publishes a **railed number wearing a ~0.05 dex bar** — strictly worse than today, where P is honestly flagged owed. Good gf lends false authority to a number whose problem was never gf. Same trap for whichever of S/N/Cu turns out to be saturation.

**RYA-752 → half superseded, keep the diagnostic half.** Its *remedy* (get better gf on N/S/Si) is this umbrella's step 1 and can retire. Its *diagnostic* must survive: the line-by-line delta against the anchor paper's own values on the overlap set is what tells you **why** a value did not move. This umbrella produces a point on a plot, not an explanation. So keep 752 as the **escalation path when a child fails to land in the band**, and fold 749/753/754 under the corresponding element children rather than running both.

One caveat on 752's premise, for when it runs: it attributes the +0.36–0.42 cluster to "non-Amarsi gf lineage," but the split it observes (C/O small, N/S/Si large) also tracks **which elements have Amarsi's NLTE grid wired**. Those two are confounded in its table, and only the line-by-line overlap separates them.

### 6. Suggested child template additions

1. **Step 0 — RYA-697 triage** (saturation / ion-label / railed / genuine gf) before any line list is touched.
2. **Exclude forbidden lines explicitly** when the element has a forbidden-line lab literature (Fe II, and this will recur for the Fe-peak and n-capture children).
3. **Report the RMS, and say so** — do not quote the median cited σ as the expected bar.
4. **Escalate to RYA-752's line-by-line diagnostic** if the value misses the band.

RATIFIED CONVENTION (amendment) -- showcase-graded / document-ungraded, per region, uniform across ALL elements

Ratified 2026-08-22. Extends the presentation convention (2026-06-18) and this umbrella's "all products shown; gold is the per-band physics/quality winner" principle onto the gf-quality axis. Applies to every element, same format.

THE FORMAT (two quality tiers, per region UV/VIS/IR):
- SHOWCASE = the graded pool (lab / NIST C+ gf). ALWAYS the reported/headline value, with its cited-sigma bar.
- DOCUMENT = the ungraded pool (Kurucz semi-empirical). Shown as a diagnostic with its honest wide bar (0.17-0.30 dex). Present, never hidden.

FIREWALL (non-negotiable, RYA-161 class):
- The reported value is ALWAYS the graded pool. Ungraded is documented, NEVER showcased, NEVER averaged into the headline, NEVER allowed to move the reported number.
- Graded and ungraded are distinct QUALITY TIERS, treated exactly like disagreeing regions (presentation spec 2026-06-18): both shown, never merged. Blending ungraded into a thin graded pool to buy statistics IS the provenance-trust failure -- forbidden.

THIN / EMPTY graded pool (handled IN-format, not special-cased):
- Thin graded (e.g. Al may be 3-5 lines): still showcase graded, honestly, with small N and its real bar. Ungraded documentation then shows whether the few graded lines are corroborated.
- Zero graded for a line/region: showcase slot reads "not established"; ungraded is documented as best-available-but-unqualified. Never silently promoted to fill the gap.

COST + PAYOFF:
- Nearly free: this is retention + presentation, not extra inversions. Keep the ungraded per-line abundances instead of discarding them post-selection.
- Emergent: because the format is identical for every element, the graded-vs-ungraded SPREAD becomes a per-element gf-limitation index. Fe = tiny spread (gf-rich); Al = large spread (gf-starved). Read across all 28 elements, that pattern is a free prioritization map for which elements this sweep should attack first.

FIRST STRESS TEST = Al. Al is funky on TWO axes at once -- thin graded gf (this axis) AND the NLTE-split near-UV resonance doublet vs the high-excitation workhorses (the engine-matrix axis). The format must document both axes without conflating them: a wide Al spread could be gf OR NLTE, and only showing both axes lets a reader tell which. Al validates the format's edge cases; Fe validates the common case.

PROPAGATION: fold into the presentation spec; flag RYA-179 for the Glossary / Method / Science Architecture doc sync. Every child of this umbrella inherits this format.

issue.description:
## Goal

Process **silicon (Si)** using the ratified all-element recipe in <issue id="f1039187-38b1-463a-98eb-ed3b4e9e7c5e" label="RYA-946" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-946/umbrella-all-element-laboratory-gf-sweep-literature-validation" />, producing defensible, provenance-complete Si line sets for the three active categories:

* **ASPLUND GRADE (**`asplund`**)** — external Solar reference line set used in the AGSS21 abundance lineage; orthogonal validation anchor.
* **CODEX GRADE (**`graded`**)** — **primary-laboratory gf only**, Solar feature depth `<= 0.60`; unsaturated/EW-valid workhorse set.
* **DEEP GRADE (**`deepgraded`**)** — **primary-laboratory gf only**, Solar feature depth `> 0.60`; same gf-quality standard, but routed to synthesis because of saturation.

Do **not** promote NIST evaluated values into Codex/Deep Grade. NIST is evidence/cross-check/future evaluated-tier material unless the project policy is explicitly changed. Do not tune gf values to reproduce AGSS21 or any other abundance.

This is a **child of** <issue id="f1039187-38b1-463a-98eb-ed3b4e9e7c5e" label="RYA-946" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-946/umbrella-all-element-laboratory-gf-sweep-literature-validation" /> and inherits its scientific method, provenance rules, all-band census, anti-tuning firewall, and freeze gate.

## Scope

Cover the Si species/indicators relevant to the Solar/FGK abundance analysis, at minimum **Si I and Si II**, and search every wavelength region actually used by the reference analyses (FUV/NUV/VIS/red optical/NIR/IR as applicable). Preserve forbidden, blended, rejected, saturated, unavailable, and otherwise excluded transitions as explicit statuses rather than silently dropping them.

### 0. Read the recipe before touching data

Read <issue id="f1039187-38b1-463a-98eb-ed3b4e9e7c5e" label="RYA-946" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-946/umbrella-all-element-laboratory-gf-sweep-literature-validation" /> **in full, including all comments/results**, and use Fe as the reference implementation. Reconcile this work with <issue id="4096f5f6-0ee8-4046-b45a-a79601ac6f1e" label="RYA-752" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-752/umbrella-systematic-gf-scale-audit-codex-kitt-peak-chain-nssi-036-042" /> (existing N/S/Si gf-scale diagnostic) rather than duplicating or losing its diagnostic findings.

### 1. Reconstruct the Asplund/AGSS21 Si reference line set

Trace the adopted Solar Si abundance in **Asplund, Amarsi & Grevesse 2021 (AGSS21)** to the actual element-specific source paper(s), table(s), supplements, catalogues, and line-level atomic data.

For every published-used or explicitly rejected Si transition, capture at minimum:

`reference_line_set | adopted_solar_value_lineage | source_paper/table/catalog | species | wavelength + medium | EP/transition identity | published loggf | published gf source | EW/profile/weight/exclusion | source band | notes`

Rules:

* Do not infer “Asplund-used” from a generic Si candidate list.
* If AGSS21 points to an earlier analysis, follow the citation chain to the primary line table.
* Verify exact bibliographic metadata/DOI and catalogue identifiers against authoritative literature services before recording them.
* If the primary line list is genuinely unavailable after checking paper, supplement, catalogue, and cited source, record `SOURCE_LINE_LIST_NOT_PUBLISHED` with the search trail.

Output this population as **ASPLUND GRADE**, keeping its published/reference gf distinct from the Codex adopted gf where they differ.

### 2. Primary-laboratory gf census — exhaustive best effort

Find **every usable Si transition with primary experimental laboratory oscillator-strength / transition-probability data** relevant to the Codex wavelength holdings, not merely the lines already in VALD or already used by AGSS21.

Search the primary literature and laboratory datasets for Si I and Si II. Establish, per source:

* exact paper / authors / year / DOI;
* laboratory method and whether the reported gf is genuinely experimental;
* wavelength/species/transition coverage;
* uncertainty per transition or the most defensible source-level uncertainty when line-level values are unavailable;
* known limitations, blends, branching-fraction/lifetime issues, or superseding measurements.

**No fabricated citations.** Every claimed primary-lab source must be verified before ingest.

### 3. Cross-check against existing atomic holdings

Crossmatch the laboratory census and AGSS21 line set against:

* Codex `canonical_gf` / current line assets;
* existing **VALD3** extraction(s);
* **NIST ASD** values/grades if already present locally; retrieve NIST if the required Si evidence is not on file.

Crossmatch through the canonical physical-transition matcher: species/ion + wavelength/frame + EP/levels/component identity — **never wavelength alone**.

For each matched transition retain both the authoritative primary-lab value and comparison values from NIST/VALD, with source provenance. Do not overwrite disagreement without adjudication.

### 4. Grade the primary-lab pool by Solar feature depth

Using the <issue id="f1039187-38b1-463a-98eb-ed3b4e9e7c5e" label="RYA-946" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-946/umbrella-all-element-laboratory-gf-sweep-literature-validation" /> ratified definitions, measure Solar feature depth consistently from the approved Solar spectrum and classify primary-lab lines:

* depth `< 0.05`: below observability floor; report separately, not active graded pool;
* depth `0.05–0.60`: **CODEX GRADE (**`graded`**)**;
* depth `> 0.60`: **DEEP GRADE (**`deepgraded`**)**, synthesis route.

Depth is the route axis, **not** a gf-quality ranking. Codex and Deep Grade require the same primary-laboratory provenance.

Document blends/contamination and any line for which depth classification is ambiguous.

### 5. Required per-line joined product

Produce a machine-readable Si table with at least:

`canonical_line_id | species | wavelength | medium/frame | EP | transition/levels | canonical_loggf | gf_tier | primary_lab_source | DOI | lab_sigma | NIST_loggf | NIST_grade | VALD_loggf/source | AGSS21/reference_used | reference_loggf | delta_reference_vs_codex | solar_feature_depth | depth_status | grade={asplund,graded,deepgraded,below_floor,ungraded} | band | blend/exclusion/status | join_status | ambiguity_note`

Keep the Asplund reference membership orthogonal: a line may be both an external reference transition and independently qualify for a Codex/Deep primary-lab pool, but the two provenance roles must remain distinguishable in the data model.

### 6. Coverage + gap accounting

Produce per-band counts/matrices for:

* AGSS21/source-used;
* AGSS21/source-explicitly-rejected;
* Codex matched;
* primary-lab gf available;
* Codex Grade;
* Deep Grade;
* below observability floor;
* evaluated/NIST-only;
* fallback/ungraded;
* missing from Codex;
* ambiguous crossmatches.

Empty graded cells are **real coverage gaps**. Never backfill them with evaluated/fallback lines merely to make the grid look complete.

### 7. Si gf-scale diagnostic / <issue id="4096f5f6-0ee8-4046-b45a-a79601ac6f1e" label="RYA-752" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-752/umbrella-systematic-gf-scale-audit-codex-kitt-peak-chain-nssi-036-042" /> reconciliation

Because Si is already implicated in <issue id="4096f5f6-0ee8-4046-b45a-a79601ac6f1e" label="RYA-752" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-752/umbrella-systematic-gf-scale-audit-codex-kitt-peak-chain-nssi-036-042" />, preserve and execute the useful diagnostic portion of that work:

* compare line-by-line `delta_loggf` on the overlap between the external reference analysis and Codex;
* test whether any abundance discrepancy is consistent with a uniform gf zero-point shift versus line-specific errors/subset selection/model physics;
* compute the applicable <issue id="3c0918f0-e567-429c-b87d-46ca2e606a15" label="RYA-987" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-987/compute-rya-968-zero-point-cap-on-the-163-line-graded-anchor-up-from-7" />/968-style zero-point cap for the Si primary-lab pool;
* do not attribute an abundance offset to gf until this separation is demonstrated.

### 8. Measurement-readiness gate

Do **not** mark Si `FROZEN_READY_FOR_MEASUREMENT` until:

1. AGSS21/reference Solar line census is complete or a documented source-publication exception is approved;
2. primary-lab gf census is best-effort exhaustive and sources are verified;
3. physical-transition crossmatches are adjudicated;
4. Codex/Deep depth grading is complete;
5. all-band gaps/ungraded remainder are explicitly documented;
6. zero-point diagnostic/cap is computed;
7. no unresolved provenance ambiguity could silently change the adopted gf scale.

## Deliverables

1. Machine-readable **Si AGSS21/reference line set** including used and rejected rows.
2. Machine-readable **Si primary-lab gf census** with uncertainties and citations.
3. Joined Si line product with **Asplund / Codex / Deep** classifications.
4. Per-band coverage/gap matrix.
5. Source-lineage note explaining how the reference lines lead to the adopted Solar Si abundance.
6. Si gf-scale / zero-point diagnostic tied back to <issue id="4096f5f6-0ee8-4046-b45a-a79601ac6f1e" label="RYA-752" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-752/umbrella-systematic-gf-scale-audit-codex-kitt-peak-chain-nssi-036-042" />.
7. Short science note listing unresolved walls, ambiguity, saturation/blend issues, and recommended next actions.
8. Reproducible scripts/tests used to build and validate every artifact.

## Scientific firewalls

* **Primary-lab gf only** for Codex Grade and Deep Grade.
* **ASPLUND GRADE is a reference membership, not a gf-quality tier.**
* Never tune gf, line selection, continuum, or model settings to force agreement with AGSS21/literature (<issue id="68caa0a1-dd50-4c03-8386-a6c7ab48d24b" label="RYA-161" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-161/science-solar-astrophysical-log-gf-calibration-blue-edge-cut" />).
* NIST/VALD disagreements are evidence to adjudicate, not permission to choose whichever value gives the preferred abundance.
* Every scientific value gets one authoritative provenance path.
* Preserve negative results and documented walls.
* IR lines cannot support an IR abundance product unless telluric correction has been verified.

## Relationship

Parent/recipe: <issue id="f1039187-38b1-463a-98eb-ed3b4e9e7c5e" label="RYA-946" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-946/umbrella-all-element-laboratory-gf-sweep-literature-validation" /> — all-element laboratory-gf sweep + literature validation.

Reference implementation: Fe workflow cited by <issue id="f1039187-38b1-463a-98eb-ed3b4e9e7c5e" label="RYA-946" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-946/umbrella-all-element-laboratory-gf-sweep-literature-validation" />.

Diagnostic predecessor to reconcile: <issue id="4096f5f6-0ee8-4046-b45a-a79601ac6f1e" label="RYA-752" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-752/umbrella-systematic-gf-scale-audit-codex-kitt-peak-chain-nssi-036-042" /> — N/S/Si gf-scale audit.

Anti-tuning: <issue id="68caa0a1-dd50-4c03-8386-a6c7ab48d24b" label="RYA-161" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-161/science-solar-astrophysical-log-gf-calibration-blue-edge-cut" />.

issue.description:
Ryan, 2026-08-09: *"we create 27 tickets, for each element, and we go through each one, and verify, rerun, give it the Al treatment. If it fails, why, and document."*

## First — "the Al treatment" needed defining, because Al is not done

Aluminium was worked hard for a full session and reached **4 of its 26 reachable lines — 15%** — with **nothing promoted to the pool**. Stamping that phrase on twenty-six elements would have industrialised a 15% pass and called it a sweep.

`docs/ELEMENT_PROTOCOL.md` (RYA-711) now defines it. **DONE = every reachable usable line has an OUTCOME**, not a value. A line that cannot be measured is done when its reason is recorded and checkable. `scripts/line_accounting_rya709.py` is the scoreboard: an element is done when `unmeasured_reachable` reaches zero.

**Al is IN PROGRESS**, not done — rung 2 blocked (no IR NLTE grid), rung 3 never run, IR cross-check not done, 22 reachable lines untouched.

## The eight gates

**ACCOUNT** → **COVER** → **MEASURE** → **GRADE** → **REACH** → **LADDER** → **CROSS-CHECK** → **REPORT**

Full text in the protocol. The ones that bite: measure on *every* covering instrument; window half-width from the **line separation**, not the FWHM; unresolved NIST components are **summed**; ungraded gf **holds** the promotion; the ladder is **executed, not narrated**; report per **(instrument × band)**.

## Three outcomes, and a fourth that is a defect

**RESOLVED** · **BOUNDED** · **UNRESOLVED**. The fourth — *unresolved where a rung was never attempted* — is a finding against the pipeline, not against the star.

## The work

**10,852 unmeasured-reachable lines across 26 elements.**

| tranche | elements | unmeasured |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **LARGE** — needs batching | Fe 4000 · Cr 1584 · Ti 1119 · Ni 819 · Co 805 · V 653 · Mn 560 | 9,540 |
| **medium** | Si 352 · Zr 280 · Ca 199 · Mg 124 | 955 |
| **small** — single session | Sc 81 · Y 64 · C 45 · Cu 38 · Na 32 · S 30 · **Al 26** · K 10 · Eu 10 · Sr 9 · Ba 6 · O 5 · P 1 | 357 |
| **acquisition only** | **Li 0 reachable** · **N 0 reachable** | — |

**Gold elements are not exempt.** Fe is frozen at gold on **223 of 4223** reachable lines and is the anchor for the entire scale. Mn 560 unmeasured, Sc 81, C 45, K 10, O 5.

## Sequencing

1. **Small tranche first** — thirteen elements, \~357 lines, and it validates the protocol at low cost before committing to Fe.
2. **Li and N** need no measurement work at all — file the acquisition requirement and close.
3. **Medium**, then **LARGE**.
4. **Fe last and deliberately.** It is the anchor; re-measuring it moves every differential abundance in the Codex. That is a decision, not a task.

## Do NOT

* Do NOT read `measured = 0` as "never measured". It counts the **EW pool only** — K, Sc, Co and N are synthesis-measured and have zero pool lines by design.
* Do NOT promote anything into `sol_ew_results_v1.csv` without the reviewed act (`promote_solar_ew.py`). Every row now requires an `instrument` stamp (RYA-710) and it is never defaulted.
* Do NOT infer an NLTE correction for any line the grid does not cover. Grid-building is future work.
* Do NOT collapse an element to one number. Per-(instrument × band) is ratified.

## The honest cost

Al's four lines produced **thirteen defects in one adapted harness**, a false NO-DATA claim that reached the state register, a duplicated instrument catalog, and six broken consumers from a CSV header. Budget for that rate rather than being surprised by it.

## 2026-09-13 protocol hardening — mandatory framework for every element from here forward

The Fe finalization, CNO publication work, and Al restart exposed several recurring failure modes that the original eight-gate protocol did not state strongly enough. From this point forward, **every canonical element must pass the same evidence → line → measurement → correction → validation → publication framework**. Existing child tickets should be interpreted through this strengthened contract; new element tickets must inherit it explicitly.

The existing `ACCOUNT → COVER → MEASURE → GRADE → REACH → LADDER → CROSS-CHECK → REPORT` structure remains valid, but each gate now carries the following mandatory requirements.

### 0. AUTHORITATIVE-STATE preflight

Before doing new scientific work:

* read the current Project Register, Target Star List, Canonical Element List, element state/register, current product feed, and active methodology/standards;
* inspect prior element tickets/results, but treat old abundance values and old classifications as historical until reproduced on the current pipeline;
* identify pipeline/schema/model/telluric/normalization blockers before manufacturing products;
* repository + authoritative data assets win over stale ticket prose.

### 1. REFERENCES — complete element literature/provenance dossier

Every element gets a verified UV/VIS/IR literature audit following the <issue id="63bfeeb4-1363-4208-ac3f-83e5f5f52d54" label="RYA-714" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-714/litscan-findings-fe-i-solar-photospheric-uvvisir-audit" />/719/720/721 family, not merely an AGSS21 citation.

Gather and verify, where applicable:

* adopted/reference Solar abundance analyses (AGSS21 plus other relevant independent modern determinations);
* line/indicator-specific Solar abundance studies;
* atomic transition-probability/gf authorities and uncertainty sources;
* HFS/isotope/component sources;
* NLTE grids/calculations and 3D/mean-3D line-formation sources;
* molecular indicator and molecular line-list sources where relevant;
* relevant UV/NIR/IR abundance studies;
* instrument/data references where scientifically material.

Every citation used in a public product must resolve through the authoritative bibliography/provenance system. Literature values are validation/comparison anchors, **never tuning targets**.

### 2. LINE CENSUS + PHYSICAL-IDENTITY AUDIT

Audit the complete scientifically relevant line/indicator census across **all bands and all applicable Solar holdings/instruments**, including atomic, forbidden, molecular, isotopologue and blend-component indicators where applicable.

For every transition preserve physical identity — species/ion, wavelength frame/medium, energy levels/EP, J/component/HFS/isotope semantics — and never promote or crossmatch by wavelength alone.

Every line must end with an explicit disposition. Coverage gaps, saturation, blends, tellurics, absent model support, and failed fits are documented outcomes, not silent omissions.

### 3. CURRENT GRADING — Reference / Codex / Deep + external lineage

Re-derive line-set membership under the **current** cross-element grading definitions. Do not inherit classifications made before Reference Grade or later grading-policy changes.

Keep separate axes for:

* atomic/molecular data provenance and uncertainty;
* **Reference Grade** membership;
* **Codex Grade** membership;
* **Deep Grade** membership;
* external/reference-study membership (AGSS21, Scott, element-specific studies, etc.);
* measurement eligibility on each holding/instrument.

These axes are not interchangeable. A high-quality reference transition may be unusable on one spectrum without losing its atomic-data grade. Conversely, observability does not make weak atomic data Reference Grade.

Reference Grade must follow the current <issue id="f1039187-38b1-463a-98eb-ed3b4e9e7c5e" label="RYA-946" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-946/umbrella-all-element-laboratory-gf-sweep-literature-validation" /> cross-element scientific policy and the best available evidence for that species; **do not assume Fe's primary-LAB implementation is universally appropriate**. CNO already demonstrates that critically evaluated theoretical data can be the correct authority.

Every graded transition requires authoritative provenance and a defensible uncertainty or an explicit unresolved/HOLD state. No blanket uncertainty placeholders where line-specific evidence exists or is required.

### 4. BAND × HOLDING/INSTRUMENT ELIGIBILITY MATRIX

For every line/indicator, audit every applicable observing path. Record at minimum coverage, route (EW/synthesis), saturation/depth, blends/components, telluric risk and actual correction state, normalization state, observed conditioning, engine/model applicability, and final eligibility/reason.

Instrument differences affect measurement eligibility, **not the intrinsic atomic/molecular grade**.

Permanent rule: **no infrared abundance is reportable unless telluric correction is verified for that exact holding/product.** Unknown telluric state is not equivalent to corrected.

### 5. MEASUREMENT — current pipeline, from scratch when provenance is stale

Measurements must be generated from current authoritative inputs, not copied from banked legacy values. If pipeline changes affect line identity, conditioning, tellurics, normalization, gf grading, uncertainties, model treatment, or product schema, rerun rather than patching the old abundance.

Maintain a per-line proof ledger carrying line ID, holding/instrument/band, line set/grade, gf source + uncertainty, route, engine/model, measurement/fit result, quality/disposition, conditioning/telluric state, and exclusion reason.

EW and synthesis are distinct scientific routes. Failed/railed/unconstrained fits are not measurements and must not emit plausible-looking abundance/uncertainty values.

### 6. ALL APPLICABLE ENGINES + PHYSICAL CORRECTIONS

For every scientifically eligible pool × band × holding, execute **every applicable validated engine/model route** rather than choosing the engine that agrees best with literature.

Depending on actual element support this may include 1D-LTE, 1D-NLTE, mean-3D/<3D>, mean-3D-NLTE, and full 3D/3D-NLTE. Label treatments exactly: never call mean-3D full 3D and never claim NLTE/3D where no validated calculation exists.

Apply all scientifically required corrections supported by the evidence/model: NLTE, 3D/mean-3D, HFS/isotope/component treatment, blends, molecular equilibrium/coupling, tellurics, continuum/normalization/conditioning, and other element-specific physics. A missing required correction becomes an explicit HOLD/limitation, not an inferred correction.

No silent engine cells. Every expected engine/model cell must contain a valid product or explicit `N/A / HOLD / FAILED` reason.

**Never average engines merely to manufacture a preferred abundance.** Engine/model products remain independent measurements/diagnostics.

### 7. UNCERTAINTY — full authoritative stack

**Canonical implementation:** <issue id="8eb95d16-a86e-4de7-86f4-b17df02b1cab" label="RYA-587" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-587/architecture-27-element-reported-uncertainty-generalization-rya-282-5" /> is the universal, element-agnostic uncertainty contract. Every current and future element child MUST invoke that recipe; do not restate a reduced local subset and do not create an element-specific replacement. Publication is gated on <issue id="8eb95d16-a86e-4de7-86f4-b17df02b1cab" label="RYA-587" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-587/architecture-27-element-reported-uncertainty-generalization-rya-282-5" />-compatible absolute uncertainty plus, for target-star abundance ratios/differentials, the matched Solar/reference differential covariance treatment.

Every abundance product must carry the current project uncertainty model and propagate the applicable components explicitly: statistical/fit or line-to-line term, gf/line-data uncertainty, stellar-parameter sensitivities, microturbulence where relevant, model/NLTE/3D terms where defined, continuum/normalization/telluric terms where scientifically required, plus total uncertainty from the authoritative component model.

Do not use zero/sentinel uncertainties for failed fits. Do not reuse obsolete fixed systematic values after the uncertainty framework changes. State assumptions/covariances and avoid double-counting correlated terms.

### 8. CROSS-CHECK / VALIDATE — never tune

Compare independent bands, holdings, instruments, routes, grades, indicators, ionization stages and engines where available. Compare against the verified literature dossier only **after** measurement.

Investigate offsets direction-first: line/gf scale, physical identity, blends/HFS, saturation, continuum/normalization, tellurics, model treatment, NLTE/3D sign/magnitude, and stellar parameters before astrophysical interpretation.

Do not tune gf, line selection, continuum, correction magnitude, or product highlighting to recover an accepted Solar abundance.

### 9. REPORT + PUBLICATION APPENDIX

Every element ultimately receives the same generated reporting architecture used for Fe/CNO:

* highlighted scientifically identified products;
* full error-bar forest with independent products preserved;
* grade/engine/indicator explanation;
* concise element context;
* complete **applicable** references for the products and claims displayed — not Asplund-only;
* problem-line/failure diagnostics;
* downloadable per-line/product data;
* downloadable element PDF generated from the same reporting data;
* reproducibility metadata (source artifacts, generator/version, git SHA, timestamp, holdings/instruments, model/engine identity).

No hand-authored scientific values in production pages/PDFs. Every publication-eligible product is visible or has a documented hide reason. Experimental/held products retain their disposition.

### 10. COMPLETENESS GATE — what `DONE` means now

An element is not scientifically complete merely because an abundance number exists. `DONE` requires:

 1. reference/literature dossier reconciled;
 2. complete line/indicator census accounted for;
 3. current Reference/Codex/Deep grading audit complete;
 4. all applicable bands + holdings/instruments audited;
 5. all scientifically eligible lines measured or explicitly dispositioned;
 6. all applicable validated engines/model treatments executed or explicitly N/A/HOLD;
 7. required corrections verified/applied or the affected product held;
 8. uncertainty stack complete;
 9. independent cross-checks/literature validation documented;
10. authoritative products + per-line proof + generated appendix/PDF/reproducibility block produced.

A blank with documented evidence can be scientifically complete. A numerical abundance produced while a required gate was skipped is **not complete**.

### Standing anti-pitfall rules learned from Fe / Al / CNO

* Do not trust legacy abundance products across material pipeline changes — reproduce them.
* Do not conflate gf provenance, Reference/Codex/Deep grade, literature membership, and measurement eligibility.
* Do not assume every element has Fe-like laboratory gf evidence.
* Do not crossmatch/promote atomic data by wavelength alone.
* Do not let instrument-level metadata stand in for holding-specific telluric/conditioning state.
* Do not report IR without verified telluric correction.
* Do not silently omit an instrument, band, indicator, engine, failed line, or unavailable model.
* Do not label mean-3D as full 3D or inferred corrections as calculated corrections.
* Do not tune to AGSS21/Lodders/other accepted values.
* Do not average engines/indicator families to hide disagreement.
* Do not publish failed fits, sentinel uncertainties, or stale ticket values as measurements.
* Do not let website/PDF references collapse to the single comparison paper when additional model/data/indicator sources actually support the result.

This hardened framework should also be reflected in `docs/ELEMENT_PROTOCOL.md` / the active successor protocol so future element tickets inherit it automatically rather than rediscovering these lessons element by element.

## 2026-09-13 mandatory Reference Documents ↔ bibliography reconciliation gate

Every element-preparation/reference-gathering ticket must update the project bibliography **during the scientific intake**, not as a publication cleanup step.

For each element:

1. Inventory the applicable files already present in the project **Reference Documents** folder before searching externally.
2. Reconcile every scientifically applicable local reference document to one canonical bibliography record.
3. For every new paper, table, supplement, atomic-data source, model paper, line-list paper, or other scientific source discovered/used during the audit, create or update the canonical bibliography entry as part of the same work.
4. Deduplicate alternate copies/citations and preserve one authoritative bibliographic identity (DOI/ADS/bibcode or equivalent authoritative identifier where available).
5. Every scientific citation/provenance key emitted by line lists, gf records, model metadata, abundance products, appendix pages, or PDFs must resolve to the canonical bibliography.
6. Conversely, applicable local Reference Documents should be traceable to their bibliography record and scientific role/usage where practical.
7. A valid scientific source does **not** require a locally archived PDF. If no legal/local copy exists, retain canonical citation/identifier/source metadata and record the local-document state rather than omitting the source.
8. Do not fabricate DOI, ADS/bibcode, journal metadata, page/table identifiers, or source lineage. If metadata cannot be verified, mark it unresolved and hold that provenance branch as needed.
9. The generated website/PDF reference list must derive from/reconcile against this canonical bibliography and product provenance rather than a hand-maintained element-specific citation list.

### Gate / Definition of Done addition

An element is not `FROZEN_READY_FOR_MEASUREMENT` / scientifically intake-complete until the applicable Reference Documents inventory and bibliography reconciliation are complete enough that every adopted gf/line-data source, NLTE/3D model source, indicator/molecular source, and literature validation source used by the measurement has a resolvable canonical citation.

Required closeout summary per element:

`reference_documents_scanned | bibliography_entries_added | bibliography_entries_updated | duplicates_reconciled | sources_without_local_copy | unresolved_metadata | provenance_keys_verified`

This is now a standing cross-element requirement and should be reflected in `docs/ELEMENT_PROTOCOL.md` / active successor protocol.

# Scope note for the sweep: Fe I gf provenance is 76% K07 semi-empirical (Claude.ai, from committed canonical_gf.csv)

Surfaced while verifying RYA-760's Fe IR gf work. Recomputed the Fe I source-provenance breakdown directly from canonical_gf.csv (15458 Fe I rows):

| source | accuracy | Fe I rows | share |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **K07 (Kurucz semi-empirical, COMPUTED)** | 0.20 | **11684** | **76%** |
| other / bare VALD3 / none | -- | 2661 | 17% |
| FMW (Fuhr Martin Wiese, NIST compilation) | 0.08 | 302 | 2% |
| BWL (Blackwell furnace) | 0.02 | 291 | 2% |
| MRW | 0.08 | 253 | 2% |
| 2014MNRAS. / GESHRL14 (Ruffoni FTS) | 0.03 | 147 | 1% |
| BK / BKK (Bard-Kock) | 0.04 | 107 | <1% |
| GESB82c | 0.08 | 13 | <1% |

**The measured/lab tier (FMW+BWL+MRW+Ruffoni+BK combined) is ~1100 lines. K07 semi-empirical is 11684.** So the whole RYA-760 FMW question (+0.29 dex on 12 IR lines) is a real but SMALL fish next to the structural reality: three-quarters of Fe I gf provenance is Kurucz COMPUTED values at 0.20 dex accuracy -- and only 8 of 15458 Fe I lines carry a NIST grade.

**Why this belongs on the sweep and not just on Fe:** every element's frontier product hits the same distribution. The near-UV/IR is where the measured sources thin out and K07 fills the gap -- exactly the bands the sweep is opening. So for most reachable frontier lines, the binding uncertainty is not NLTE (0.05 dex) or the measurement -- it is a 0.20-dex semi-empirical gf that does not average down (a scale systematic, RYA-161). Two consequences worth a sweep-level decision:

1. The per-element frontier error budget must carry the K07 systematic as a floor term wherever the pool is K07-dominated -- not sigma/sqrt(N).
2. Grading/re-sourcing effort should be prioritized by K07 share x science leverage, not by chasing individual compilation offsets like FMW. FMW is 2% of Fe; the 76% is where the uncertainty lives.

Not proposing a ticket here -- this is a scope input to the sweep's planning. Recorded so it is visible before the per-element budgets are set. (Fe-specific follow-ons from the same verification: RYA-780 FMW adjudication, RYA-781 MRW catalogue split, RYA-782 REW trend.)

## 2026-09-15 STAT DIRECTIVE — THIS IS THE UNIVERSAL ELEMENT UNCERTAINTY CONTRACT

This ticket is the existing cross-element generalization; do NOT create a competing uncertainty framework. <issue id="d617c30e-7b0f-4c75-a40f-b0defeb06d20" label="RYA-1213" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-1213/reference-grade-complete-build-reference-products-from-all-450-lab-fe" /> proved the per-product/pool perturbation machinery on Fe, including the completed shell ξ campaign whose RESULTS must be audited rather than assumed absent. Mean-3D Gerber is experimental and is NOT a completeness requirement unless separately ratified as publication-grade.

**Scope correction:** this protocol is ELEMENT-AGNOSTIC and PRODUCT-AGNOSTIC. It must apply to Fe, Al, Si, C/N/O, and every future element/indicator/holding. Element tickets may add physics-specific terms, but may not omit this base contract.

### Required authoritative uncertainty recipe per publication-eligible product

1. **Statistical / measurement term:** line-to-line scatter / √N for vetted independent line pools where valid; fit/profile likelihood or χ²-derived uncertainty for synthesis/molecular products; explicitly flag small-N and correlated-pixel/line cases.
2. **Atomic/molecular data:** propagate line-specific gf/transition-data uncertainty from the authoritative grade/provenance model. No blanket placeholder where line-specific evidence exists. Account for covariance when a common gf scale/source affects multiple lines.
3. **Stellar-parameter perturbations:** re-derive the product at the star's sourced ±1σ Teff, log g, ξmic where physically applicable, and \[M/H\]/\[Fe/H\] where the model/product depends on it. Sensitivities belong to the actual product/line/indicator pool; do not borrow Fe or sibling-tier derivatives. 3D routes with no ξ parameter record ξ as N/A, not zero.
4. **Observation/reduction terms where applicable:** continuum/normalization, EW/profile measurement, pseudo-continuum, telluric residuals (mandatory for IR), instrumental/holding conditioning. Quantify rather than narrate where feasible.
5. **Model/physics terms where defined:** NLTE correction/grid/interpolation uncertainty, 3D/mean-3D model uncertainty, HFS/isotopic/component treatment, blends, molecular-equilibrium/coupling (especially C-N-O), and other element-specific physics. Do not invent a term when no defensible uncertainty model exists; mark unresolved/HOLD if scientifically material.
6. **Covariance:** do not blindly quadrature-sum correlated terms. Preserve/propagate known covariance among stellar parameters, common atomic-data scales, coupled molecular abundances, and derived ratios. State independence assumptions where covariance is unavailable.
7. **Differential abundance requirement:** before any target-star \[X/H\], \[X/Fe\], C/O, etc. is published, compute the differential uncertainty on matched line/indicator + engine/model routes against the Solar/reference anchor. Propagate covariance/cancellation explicitly; do NOT obtain differential σ by naively adding two independent absolute budgets. Retain both absolute A(X) uncertainty and differential uncertainty/provenance.
8. **Reported fields:** preserve component terms + provenance + applicability state and compute the authoritative `sigma_reported`/total only from measured/defined components. Missing required terms make the product HOLD/INCOMPLETE, never silently zero.

### Immediate audit / implementation deliverable

Audit <issue id="519b4513-a369-40db-89b2-59a69091840f" label="RYA-282" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-282/architecture-standard-reported-uncertainty-layer-fe-sn-stellar" />, 283, 1120, 1213, 158, 1088/1089 and current pipeline implementation against the recipe above. Reuse what exists; identify only genuine gaps. Specifically inspect the completed <issue id="d617c30e-7b0f-4c75-a40f-b0defeb06d20" label="RYA-1213" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-1213/reference-grade-complete-build-reference-products-from-all-450-lab-fe" /> ξ shell outputs and verify ingestion/product stamping. Produce one canonical machine-readable uncertainty schema/API used by all element pipelines, not element-specific copies.

Then audit the ACTIVE element work (Al, Si, CNO including <issue id="7b0d27fc-4b1a-49d0-b0dc-2ab2a70be715" label="RYA-1214" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-1214/cno-product-campaign-adjudicate-the-nisttachiev-gf-into-canonical-gf" /> and N <issue id="7cbd3810-4c68-4fc5-97e3-1219128030be" label="RYA-1220" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-1220/nitrogen-method-adjudication-literature-deep-audit-of-n-i-vs-cnnh" />) and patch their product gates so none can publish without invoking this canonical recipe. Future element children of <issue id="be8bf507-78b1-4ec2-a238-f33af47d19cf" label="RYA-709" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-709/umbrella-the-26-element-sweep-every-element-gets-the-protocol-10852" />/946 inherit it automatically.

**Definition of done:** one canonical recipe documented + implemented; Fe regression passes; <issue id="d617c30e-7b0f-4c75-a40f-b0defeb06d20" label="RYA-1213" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-1213/reference-grade-complete-build-reference-products-from-all-450-lab-fe" /> ξ results audited; Al/Si/CNO/N explicitly wired; differential covariance path defined and tested; every publication product can prove component provenance/applicability; no duplicate uncertainty definitions.

## 1. Context

This is the <issue id="519b4513-a369-40db-89b2-59a69091840f" label="RYA-282" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-282/architecture-standard-reported-uncertainty-layer-fe-sn-stellar" /> **§5 follow-up** ("extend the reported-uncertainty layer to all canonical elements"), explicitly scoped there but never ticketed.
