Fe is the sole complete budget; the `changed_vs_flat` set (C/K/Mn/O/Sc/V) flips PASS→OWED purely because these terms aren't committed. This ticket commits them per element so σ\_recon (<issue id="ea1cd998-e9c8-463f-b568-c5afdcfad874" label="RYA-586" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-586/science-arch-dynamic-per-element-reconciliation-band-replace-flat-tol" />) can read a real budget.

**Depends on** <issue id="519b4513-a369-40db-89b2-59a69091840f" label="RYA-282" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-282/architecture-standard-reported-uncertainty-layer-fe-sn-stellar" /> **(Fe layer) landing first** — that validates the machinery against Amarsi+2022 before it's generalized. **Gates the Procyon rerun:** σ\_stellar (the parameter-perturbation term) DOMINATES for F-stars, so without per-element σ\_stellar the Procyon in-bounds/questionable/garbage classification is undefined for exactly the star that needs it.

## 2. Spec

Generalize the <issue id="519b4513-a369-40db-89b2-59a69091840f" label="RYA-282" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-282/architecture-standard-reported-uncertainty-layer-fe-sn-stellar" /> Fe machinery to all 26 canonical species, writing per-element rows into the committed uncertainty artifact (`data/audit/uncertainty/solar_uncertainty_rya158.json`, the file <issue id="ea1cd998-e9c8-463f-b568-c5afdcfad874" label="RYA-586" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-586/science-arch-dynamic-per-element-reconciliation-band-replace-flat-tol" /> reads):

Report raw σ, N, σ\_stat separately (the <issue id="519b4513-a369-40db-89b2-59a69091840f" label="RYA-282" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-282/architecture-standard-reported-uncertainty-layer-fe-sn-stellar" /> two-quantity discipline). Honest caveat flagged where N=2–3 (statistically weak).
* **σ\_stellar per element** = perturb Teff, log g, ξ\_mic (and \[Fe/H\] where relevant) each by their adopted 1σ, re-derive A(X), quadrature-sum the responses. **Per element** — some species are far more Teff-/ξ-sensitive than Fe. Source the 1σ parameter uncertainties from the single declared star-parameter record; STOP-and-report if absent for a star (no guessed uncertainties).
* **Channel-aware:** EW-pool, HFS-synthesis, kittpeak, and CNO-synthesis elements compute σ\_stat differently (line scatter vs synthesis χ²) — follow the <issue id="519b4513-a369-40db-89b2-59a69091840f" label="RYA-282" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-282/architecture-standard-reported-uncertainty-layer-fe-sn-stellar" /> §5 synthesis-vs-EW sub-question; record which form each element used.
* Persist per element: raw σ, N, σ\_stat, ΔA_Teff/logg/ξ/\[Fe/H\], σ\_stellar, + provenance. Do NOT touch the raw-σ gate (<issue id="012b3cf1-c821-4e01-9cf8-07abf875ad85" label="RYA-277" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-277/architecture-per-spectral-type-acceptance-profiles-thresholds-are-a" />) — this is the additive reported layer.

**Validate-don't-tune / delta-blind:** these are error terms, computed with no reference to Δ-vs-Asplund. They feed σ\_recon's blind budget.

## 3. Smoke Test

```

python3 -m pipeline.reconciliation_band            # complete_budget now ⊋ {Fe}; the all-4 set shrinks
```

Required evidence: solar_uncertainty rows populated for all 26 (no placeholders); Fe row unchanged vs <issue id="519b4513-a369-40db-89b2-59a69091840f" label="RYA-282" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-282/architecture-standard-reported-uncertainty-layer-fe-sn-stellar" /> (regression); the <issue id="ea1cd998-e9c8-463f-b568-c5afdcfad874" label="RYA-586" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-586/science-arch-dynamic-per-element-reconciliation-band-replace-flat-tol" /> `diff_summary.incomplete_budget` list shrinks to only the genuinely-unmeasured (owed-no-value) elements; each element names which σ\_stat form (scatter vs χ²) it used. Report the before/after complete-budget set.

## 4. End-of-Session Requirements

> Post a Linear comment with: the committed per-element budget table (raw σ, N, σ\_stat, σ\_stellar, dominant param); confirmation Fe is unchanged (<issue id="519b4513-a369-40db-89b2-59a69091840f" label="RYA-282" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-282/architecture-standard-reported-uncertainty-layer-fe-sn-stellar" /> regression); the <issue id="ea1cd998-e9c8-463f-b568-c5afdcfad874" label="RYA-586" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-586/science-arch-dynamic-per-element-reconciliation-band-replace-flat-tol" /> complete-budget delta (before {Fe} → after); which elements remain OWED and why (unmeasured, not un-budgeted); branch/SHA. issue.title: Science: Solar astrophysical log gf calibration + blue-edge cut + saturation weighting
issue.description:
**Context from ChatGPT analysis of sol_ew_results_v1.csv + science architecture discussion.**

The ChatGPT analysis of the actual solar EW data confirmed that the EW engine is working — 444 Fe lines, median χ² ≈ 0.005. The pipeline has reached the point where astrophysical systematics dominate over implementation bugs. This issue captures the three highest-ROI improvements identified.

---

## Problem 1: Static log gf values are the dominant abundance error source

With 444 Fe lines the scatter averages out, but for elements with 2–4 lines (C, P, O), a single bad log gf shifts the abundance by 0.5–2 dex. The solution used by high-precision differential studies (σ ≈ 0.02–0.05 dex) is **astrophysical log gf calibration**.

### Method

For each line in the solar spectrum:

```python
# Known: A(X)_solar from Asplund 2021
# Measured: EW from solar_ew.csv
# Invert the COG to get: log_gf_astro that produces correct A(X) at known solar params
log_gf_astro = invert_COG(EW_measured, A_solar, Teff, logg, vturb, EP)

# Store correction:
delta_log_gf = log_gf_astro - log_gf_VALD
```

Lines with `|delta_log_gf| > 0.3` dex flagged as unreliable — either blend, bad VALD value, or saturation.

### Output

Add `log_gf_astro` and `delta_log_gf` columns to `linelist_solar.csv`. When the same lines are used for 55 Cnc A and Alpha Cen A, use `log_gf_astro` instead of VALD values → eliminates systematic log gf error via solar differential calibration.

This is the single highest-impact improvement available to the current pipeline.

---

## Problem 2: Blue-edge lines (< 4500 Å) are corrupting element averages

From analysis of the EW CSV:

* Cr at \~4028 Å: EW_err = 102 mÅ (unusable)
* Mn at \~4030 Å: EW_err = 20 mÅ
* Zr at \~4024 Å: EW_err = 16 mÅ

These lines are in HARPS' blue edge where SNR drops and blending explodes. They're pulling element mean abundances away from the true value.

### Fix

Add hard wavelength cut to `_build_worklist()` in `lines_fit.py`:

```python
BLUE_EDGE_EXCLUDE_A = 4500.0  # configurable in constants.py

# In _build_worklist:
clean = clean[clean['wavelength_air_A'] >= BLUE_EDGE_EXCLUDE_A]
# Special measures still bypass this (force-measured with flag)
```

Add `blue_edge_excluded` count to the worklist summary print.

---

## Problem 3: Saturated lines (EW > 100–120 mÅ) are entering the abundance average equally weighted

From the EW CSV:

* Zr median EW: 165 mÅ (heavily saturated)
* Na median EW: 161 mÅ (Na D — dominated by damping wings)
* Ba median EW: 121 mÅ

At EW > \~100 mÅ the line enters the saturation/flat part of the curve of growth, where EW becomes insensitive to abundance changes and microturbulence sensitivity explodes. These lines should have drastically reduced weight, not equal weight.

### Fix

The `line_quality_weight` in `loader.py` already has a `saturation_penalty` — confirm it's tuned to give near-zero weight at EW > 120 mÅ:

```python
# In loader.py saturation_penalty:
df['saturation_penalty'] = np.exp(-5 * (depth - 0.6).clip(lower=0))
# Verify this maps to weight ≈ 0.05 for EW ~ 150 mÅ
```

Cross-check: after fixing [loader.py](<http://loader.py>) (<issue id="846e2b53-cdda-4c84-8118-20a0d7a3bc00" label="RYA-155" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-155/bug-loaderpy-fix-syntax-error-duplicate-blend-score-and-double-return" />), run `load_linelist()` and print `line_quality_weight` distribution for Na and Ba — should be << 1.0.

---

## Validation

After all three fixes, re-run the diagnostic plots (<issue id="e42180b0-1c1f-4c97-bf2a-ecd8a97a5072" label="RYA-160" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-160/science-solar-abundance-diagnostic-plots-fe-excitation-reduced-ew" />). Expected improvement:

* Fe I excitation slope should move toward 0 (once log gf_astro applied)
* Blue-edge scatter should disappear from the wavelength plot
* Element abundance scatter should decrease for multi-line elements

**Depends on:** <issue id="846e2b53-cdda-4c84-8118-20a0d7a3bc00" label="RYA-155" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-155/bug-loaderpy-fix-syntax-error-duplicate-blend-score-and-double-return" /> (loader fixes), <issue id="e42180b0-1c1f-4c97-bf2a-ecd8a97a5072" label="RYA-160" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-160/science-solar-abundance-diagnostic-plots-fe-excitation-reduced-ew" /> (diagnostic plots to validate before/after)

The frozen-gold S stays LOW_CONFIDENCE 7.753 until that re-anchoring lands → then S banks at its correct differential value.

|---|---|---|

Costa Silva's 7.12 is a MOOG+Kurucz-ATLAS-tuned differential zero-point that does not transfer to our Turbospectrum+MARCS+IAG engine.

### What this means for RYA-161

### The 161 question for S (when this ticket runs)

S forms its Mult. 8 lines high-excitation (χ ~7.87 eV) + deep — candidate causes to partition: (a) MARCS vs Kurucz-ATLAS model-atmosphere structure at those depths; (b) our IAG continuum vs their Kurucz-atlas continuum placement; (c) the Korotin NLTE (<0.1, applied) leaving a residual. **Cross-ref:** RYA-492 (the disproof + the banked CS gf), RYA-466 (Cu — the sibling residual), RYA-398/399 (gf-floor budgeting), RYA-491 (where S +0.40 was first surfaced), RYA-488 (S-in-HARPS scoping). S = the α-element gf-floor case; rides the same calibration pass as the iron-peak metals.

The solar absolute residual (Cr +0.40, etc.) is a *real* physical floor (gf-zero-point + 1D→3D + NLTE) and must NOT be erased by solar-calibrated gf.

**The legitimate, firewall-compliant version** (per RYA-398/399): astrophysical log-gf is **differential-survey-only**. Compute the per-line gf correction on the Sun, then apply it **differentially** to the targets (55 Cnc / α Cen / Procyon), where the *systematic* gf error cancels in [X/H]. It is a **target-precision tool executed on the benchmark track — NOT a solar-completion task.** It does not, and must not, change the solar verdict.

Rescope to: "Differential gf calibration for the benchmark/target track." The solar COG inversion is the *calibration step*; the *payoff* is differential precision on the targets; the solar absolute residual stays documented (escalated, never erased). Belongs with the Procyon/α Cen differential work, not the solar baseline.

Parked → Backlog, priority Urgent→Medium. Superseded-in-part by RYA-395/398/456; live core (differential gf) deferred to the benchmark track. Related: RYA-398, RYA-399, RYA-395, RYA-456.

## Scope boundary — 161 is the differential-survey gf path, NOT a solar-validation escalation

Flagging so this doesn't get misapplied: 161's astrophysical gf inverts the COG with the known Asplund abundance, so it makes the **solar** metal abundances reproduce Asplund *by construction*. That's correct and powerful for the **differential survey** (55 Cnc / α Cen), where the gf error is common-mode Sun↔target and cancels in [X/H] — but it is **circular/tuning if used in the solar validation** (RYA-371/239).

issue.title: INGEST: Fe I/II laboratory gf into canonical_gf (O'Brian/NIST-C+, Den Hartog 2014, Ruffoni 2014, Belmonte 2017; Fe II Den Hartog 2019)
issue.description:
## 1. Context

Audit this session: `data/linelists/canonical_gf.csv` (167,739 rows) is dominated by VALD3 (\~41k) and Kurucz vintages (K07/K09/K10/K13, \~75k combined). **Ruffoni 2014 (**`RU`**) is partially wired; O'Brian 1991 and Den Hartog 2014 Fe I lab gf are ABSENT.** The ungraded Kurucz pool carries a measured +0.10 dex zero-point offset (<issue id="0c807ff4-2585-4977-a054-a8b04152a1f1" label="RYA-819" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-819/reconcile-gold-anchors-magic-2013-1d-3d-correction-005-vs-amarsi-2022" />/831): the 148-line VIS Fe I pool reads 7.586 while the 9-line lab-gf pool reads 7.445 (on Asplund 7.46). That gap is atomic-data, not measurement — every engine/telluric fix sits under it (<issue id="d644fd7f-6ac5-4948-b701-48aa3fb799a4" label="RYA-855" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-855/fix-derive-band-products-hardcodes-gf-gradedfalse-at-both-call-sites" /> moved 0/36 bars).

The field's solar Fe uses **NIST grade C or better (<=0.12 dex, mostly O'Brian 1991) + Den Hartog 2014 + Ruffoni 2014 (lab, <=0.02 dex), EP >= 1.2 eV**, with **Fe II from Den Hartog 2019** (NOT Melendez & Barbuy 2009, which is solar-fitted -> firewalled, <issue id="68caa0a1-dd50-4c03-8386-a6c7ab48d24b" label="RYA-161" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-161/science-solar-astrophysical-log-gf-calibration-blue-edge-cut" />). This ticket ingests that backbone into `canonical_gf` so the reported Fe value lands in the literature band by construction, not by offset cancellation.

**Fe first, thoroughly, no cherry-picking** — ingest the full lab set. This is the template for the later all-element sweep; get it right here. Do NOT re-run abundances in this ticket.

Related: <issue id="63bfeeb4-1363-4208-ac3f-83e5f5f52d54" label="RYA-714" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-714/litscan-findings-fe-i-solar-photospheric-uvvisir-audit" />, <issue id="0c807ff4-2585-4977-a054-a8b04152a1f1" label="RYA-819" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-819/reconcile-gold-anchors-magic-2013-1d-3d-correction-005-vs-amarsi-2022" />/831, <issue id="a93ba5bf-5b56-42fe-9610-56e51df57d19" label="RYA-822" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-822/build-extend-adjudicate-canonical-gf-blueward-of-3780-a-the-near-uv-fe" />/834 (canonical_gf precedence machinery), <issue id="d1add25a-194e-4217-9600-9357c95597aa" label="RYA-824" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-824/build-primary-lab-gf-fe-sub-pool-re-measure-every-fe-line-that-has-a" />/852 (prior Fe lab-gf sub-pool), <issue id="68caa0a1-dd50-4c03-8386-a6c7ab48d24b" label="RYA-161" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-161/science-solar-astrophysical-log-gf-calibration-blue-edge-cut" /> (validate-don't-tune firewall).

## 2. Spec

Extend `canonical_gf` via the EXISTING precedence machinery — `scripts/rya822_extend_canonical_gf.py` and `scripts/rya834_extend_canonical_gf_redward.py`. Follow that pattern; do NOT reinvent it.

**Fe I sources to ingest (all crossmatch-verified by air wavelength + excitation potential):**

1. **NIST ASD Fe I, grade C or better** (<=0.12 dex) — the O'Brian 1991 backbone as curated by NIST. Pull via NIST ASD; stamp `nist_grade` from ASD; `loggf_reference='NIST-C+'` (or the per-line NIST-listed source).
2. **Den Hartog et al. 2014, ApJS 215, 23** — VizieR **J/ApJS/215/23** (astroquery). \~203 lab lines, <=0.02 dex. tag `DH14`. DOI 10.1088/0067-0049/215/2/23.
3. **Ruffoni et al. 2014, MNRAS 441, 3127** (GES Fe I) — VERIFY the existing `RU` rows against the published table; fill any gaps. tag `RU14`. DOI 10.1093/mnras/stu780.
4. **Belmonte et al. 2017, ApJ 848, 125** (Fe I high-lying odd-parity) — VizieR J/ApJ/848/125. tag `BEL17`. DOI 10.3847/1538-4357/aa8cd3.

**Fe II source:** **Den Hartog et al. 2019** (ApJS, Fe II UV/blue lab gf) — already in `bibliography.csv` as `den_hartog_2019`; ingest its table. tag `DH19`. **Do NOT use Melendez & Barbuy 2009 for Fe II abundance (firewalled).**

**Precedence (highest to lowest):** lab (DH14 / RU14 / BEL17 / DH19) > NIST grade A/B/C > Kurucz K## > VALD3. Record `loggf_reference` + `nist_grade` + `seed_source` per line. **A lab value is NEVER overwritten by Kurucz or VALD.**

**Crossmatch rules:** match on air wavelength within <=5 mA AND excitation_potential within \~0.05 eV (both, to prevent mis-assignment). Be HFS-aware — do not merge/split HFS components. Where several lab sources give the same line, apply precedence AND record the inter-source spread as a diagnostic. VERIFY each match; **loud-fail on any ambiguous match — never silently pick** (this is the provenance-trust failure class).

**Diagnostic-line flag** (do NOT delete other lines — flag only): a line is abundance-diagnostic if it has reliable gf (lab or NIST C+), EP >= 1.2 eV (lines below bias high), and is not blend-flagged. This flag defines the pool the derive step will later report from.

Permanent rules: no fabricated values; every ingested gf carries source + grade + DOI; no silent fallbacks; VALD/Kurucz never override lab.

## 3. Smoke Test

```
      and float(r['excitation_potential_eV'] or 0)>=1.2]
print("Fe I diagnostic lines (lab/NIST-C+, EP>=1.2):", len(diag))     # expect >> 9, into the hundreds
# no lab value overwritten by Kurucz/VALD
bad=[r for r in rows if isFeI(r) and r['loggf_reference'].startswith(('K','VALD')) and r['seed_source'] in lab]
assert not bad, f"PRECEDENCE VIOLATION: {len(bad)} lab lines overwritten"
for r in diag[:5]: print(r['wavelength_air_A'], r['excitation_potential_eV'], r['log_gf'], r['loggf_reference'], r['nist_grade'])
PY
```

Expected: Fe I diagnostic count jumps from \~9 (VIS) into the hundreds across bands; zero precedence violations; 5 sample lab-graded lines print with source + grade.

## 3. Per-source counts ingested

| tag | source | DOI / access | in table | matched | **adopted** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DH14` | Den Hartog+ 2014, ApJS 215, 23 | `10.1088/0067-0049/215/2/23` · VizieR **J/ApJS/215/23** | 203 | 199 | **199** |

| `NIST-C+` | NIST ASD via `astroquery.nist` | `physics.nist.gov/asd` | 2,180 graded C+ | — | **1,202** |

Fe I ASD coverage is now **continuous 3000–12935 Å**; Fe II ASD is the repo's first, **3000–10502 Å**.

### 🔴 Den Hartog 2019 is not on VizieR — VERIFIED, not assumed

`Vizier.get_catalogs('J/ApJS/243/33')` returns **0 tables**; `cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/ftp/J/ApJS/243/33/` is a hard **404**; **arXiv:1907.11760 is a PDF-only submission**, so the Belmonte LaTeX-source route does not exist either. Parsed from the published PDF with four controls: **131 rows vs the 131 the caption states**, 0 duplicate wavelengths, 0 rows with E_upper ≤ E_lower, and **level splitting reproducing the quoted wavelength to 1.65e-06 eV**.

⚠️ pypdf renders that paper's `±` as the private-use pair **U+F0A0**, so a regex written against the characters you *see* matched **zero** rows. The count control is the only reason a silent empty parse became a loud one.

---

## 4. 🔴 The ticket's `RU` premise is a reference-code collision

The ticket says Ruffoni 2014 (`RU`) is partially wired. **It is not wired at all under that code.**

- All **5,113** `RU` rows are **Fe II** — plus Cr II. Ruffoni 2014 is an **Fe I** paper.
- VALD's own reference block, read from `VALD/Procyon/RyanSchmitt.019514`: **`Fe 2: Raassen & Uylings … gf:RU`**. `RU` is a theoretical orthogonal-operator calculation.
- Ruffoni's Fe I values *do* reach `canonical_gf`, under the GES codes **`GESHRL14`** and the truncated bibcode **`2014MNRAS.`**.

Treating `RU` as "lab already wired" would have credited **5,113 theoretical Fe II rows as primary laboratory data**. Pinned by test so it cannot regress.

### Ticket item 3, answered from the data

Do the rows `canonical_gf` *already* attributes to a lab paper carry that paper's number? A reference code is a claim; the delta is the check.

| existing reference | n | median Δ | max \|Δ\| | agree ≤0.02 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2014MNRAS.` (Ruffoni) | 81 | +0.000 | 0.040 | **74** |
| `GESHRL14` (Den Hartog) | 57 | +0.000 | 0.250 | 39 |
| `BWL+GESHRL` | 25 | +0.006 | 0.086 | 15 |
| `VALD3` | 122 | +0.017 | **2.961** | 24 |
| `NIST ASD … T5720` | 44 | −0.025 | 0.635 | 6 |

Ruffoni's existing rows check out (74/81). The GES-coded Den Hartog rows are 39/57 — the residual is RYA-799's SCALE-MISMATCH class, and this ingest fixes it by writing the paper's own value.

---

## 5. Crossmatch: ambiguities and how resolved

**Zero ambiguous matches.** Every one that could have been is reported, none guessed.

| | Fe I | Fe II |
|---|---|---|
| lab lines | 465 | 131 |
| matched | **402 (86.5 %)** | **22 (16.8 %)** |
| ambiguous (>1 candidate) | **0** | **0** |
| absent | 63 | 109 |
| randomised null | **0.04 %** | **0.0 %** |

### 🔴 The wavelength window is MEASURED, not chosen

Binning the 2,023 graded NIST matches by wavelength residual and asking how often the two sources then disagree by more than 0.2 dex:

| residual (Å) | n | frac \|Δ\| > 0.2 dex | median \|Δ\| |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 – 0.001 | 1783 | 1.9 % | 0.0003 |
| 0.001 – 0.003 | 184 | 3.8 % | 0.0009 |
| 0.003 – 0.006 | 29 | 3.4 % | 0.0006 |
| 0.006 – 0.012 | 17 | **11.8 %** | 0.0025 |
| 0.012 – 0.020 | 10 | **30.0 %** | **0.1201** |

The last two bins are a **different population** — RYA-822's chance-pairing signature, where coincidences pile up at the tolerance *wall* while real matches sit at the fourth decimal. Window set inside that separation, at **the ticket's 5 mÅ**, which the data independently vindicates. It costs 27 of 2,023 graded matches (1.3 %) and removes the contaminated tail.

### Other refusals, all reported

- **1 lab line** fell on a multi-component canonical row — **HFS refusal**: a per-transition lab gf cannot replace a gf-summed one.
- **6 ASD rows** share a canonical row with another ASD row ⇒ neither identifies it, both refused.
- **560 candidate rewrites refused** as tier downgrades or lateral moves (28 LAB→LAB are RYA-834's, untouched by design).

### ⚠️ Inter-source spread has an EMPTY population, and that is a fact about the sources

The ticket asks for it as a diagnostic. **No canonical row is measured by more than one lab paper** — the three Fe I sets are disjoint by construction: DH14 is high-lying **even**-parity, BEL17 high-lying **odd**-parity, RU14 the GES set.

### 🔴 RYA-834's band-specific ruling overrules this ticket's blanket precedence

In 9199.9–12935 Å, RYA-834 measured ASD against the band's own line list: 34 of 56 matched, **median |Δ| 0.0003 dex**. That is the same number arriving twice (RYA-760), so there NIST is **recorded, never adopted**. Honoured here: **24 rows take the grade and its σ without their value moving.** A band-specific measurement outranks a general rule. Its test caught me the first time I did not.

### ⚠️ 58 outliers, every one on a ledger

Per TP reference the NIST-minus-incumbent delta is **median 0.000, MAD 0.000–0.002** — this ingest is very largely a **null on values**. 58 rows move by more than the 0.20 dex Kurucz systematic; all are in `outlier_ledger.csv`. Largest:

| species | λ (Å) | EP | old | new | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fe I | 5487.738 | 2.18 | −6.643 (K07) | −1.994 (NIST-C+, grade C) | **+4.649** |
| Fe I | 8432.174 | 3.88 | −5.755 (K07) | −1.770 (RU14) | +3.985 |
| Fe II | 6841.663 | 11.23 | −2.692 (RU) | +0.441 (NIST-C+, B+) | +3.133 |
| Fe I | 3026.056 | 2.18 | −5.038 (VALD3) | −2.077 (BEL17) | +2.961 |

Both top cases were re-queried against **live ASD** and are internally consistent with their own A-values (5487.738: f_ik 0.00145, g_i 7 ⇒ log gf −1.994; an **intercombination** transition, where a Kurucz semi-empirical value is exactly what you would expect to be wrong). Match residuals for these are ≤0.003 Å / ≤0.0004 eV — real identifications, real source disagreement.

### ⚠️ Nine pre-existing rows demoted, not papered over

My own test found them. `demoted_nist_rows.csv`:
- **5** carry a per-transition ASD gf on a **2-component HFS cluster** (RYA-822) — the same error this script refuses to make on the way in.
- **4** carry a stored `NIST ASD v5.11 grade A/B` with no verified σ (RYA-354). **RYA-852 already showed two are stale**: 6149.246 and 6247.557 stored as B while live ASD reports **E (0.301)** and **D (0.176)** — understated **7.3×** and **4.3×**. Re-deriving a σ from the stored letter would launder that staleness into a number.

Demoted to `OTHER`: value and note kept, **claim** withdrawn.

---

## 6. Smoke test output — verbatim

The ticket's script reads `r['loggf_reference'] in {'DH14',…}`, but `loggf_reference` keeps the repo's existing `PRIMARY LAB <Source>` wording, which `test_redward_gf_extension_rya834` asserts on and `generate_sources_page.py` renders. The ticket's short tags live in the new **`lab_source_tag`** column. Only that column name differs from the ticket's text; the logic is unchanged.

```
Fe I diagnostic lines (lab/NIST-C+, EP>=1.2): 1364
precedence violations: 0
3781.1861 2.1979 -1.9393 NIST-C+ T5720 C 0.0969
3782.4478 2.998 -1.7518 NIST-C+ T5720 C 0.0969
3785.706 3.2367 -1.3755 NIST-C+ T5720 C+ 0.0719
3785.9479 2.4327 -0.9374 NIST-C+ T5720 B+ 0.0294
3789.1755 2.7275 -1.33 PRIMARY LAB Belmonte2017  0.03
```

(1,364 is the ticket's own Fe I-only, `nist_grade in (A,A+,B,C)` filter; the full Fe I+II diagnostic flag is **1,826**.)

---

## 7. Two things unblocked en route

**`coverage.load_registry` was broken on main.** It fed every holding's `manifest_path` to `read_csv`, and **RYA-929 and RYA-931 both registered a JSON intake manifest**, so it died with `Expected 2 fields in line 7, saw 3` — a tokenizer message naming neither the file nor the registry, so it reads as data corruption rather than a format assumption. It took out **every caller**, `scripts/line_accounting_rya709.py` among them. The "not a spectrum-location manifest" skip already in that loop was the right idea; it simply never ran, because the parse raised first. Extended by suffix, so a `.csv` that will not parse is still a loud failure.

**RYA-825's two-sided drift guard fired as designed** once `canonical_gf` moved: 197 of 10,215 accounting rows reported a `log_gf` that was no longer the resolver's. Regenerated on Sirius — **197 in / 197 out**, with `summary.csv` and `thresholds.json` byte-identical, so the line population and every coverage verdict are untouched and only the gf column moved.

---

## 8. Limits, stated

- **Fe II lab coverage is 22 lines and the binding constraint is OUR BLUE EDGE, not the source.** **109 of DH19's 131 lines lie blueward of `canonical_gf`'s 3000.06 Å edge.** Of the 22 reachable, **22 matched** — a 100 % hit rate on what could be reached. Extending the table below 3000 Å would make ~109 more available; that is a follow-on, not this ticket.
- **63 Fe I lab lines found no canonical row** (BEL17 46, RU14 13, DH14 4) — mostly Belmonte's deep-UV lines below 3000 Å, same edge.
- **The diagnostic flag carries two of the three criteria.** `blend_flag` is a column of the **measured EW table**, set per observation by the fitter and applied by `abundances_derive._prefilter`. A line list cannot carry it. The line-level criterion used here is the problem-children registry's standing `exclude` rows; the measurement-time filter still runs downstream. Not silently narrowed — recorded in the summary JSON.
- **Nothing was re-derived**, per the ticket. Whether the reported Fe value now lands in the literature band **by construction** is the next ticket's measurement, not this one's claim.

---

## 9. Owed / next

1. **Re-derive the Fe products on the new backbone** — the payoff test. RYA-855's "0 of 36 bars move" should now be testable properly, since ~1,600 lines carry a cited σ instead of the 0.20 blanket.
2. **Extend `canonical_gf` below 3000 Å** to reach DH19's other 109 Fe II lines and Belmonte's deep-UV Fe I.
3. **The 58-row outlier ledger wants adjudication** — each is a genuine Kurucz/VALD-vs-graded-experiment disagreement, several on lines that now enter the diagnostic pool.
4. **`pipeline/gf_rung.py`'s `LAB_GRADED_SPECIES` is still `{("Fe","I")}`** — Fe II now has a primary lab table (DH19) and could be added. Deliberately not done here: it would change what the grader referees, which is a product decision.
5. **Bibliography audit** flags two library documents with no row: `HARPS-telluric-STOP-2026-08-19.md` and `TICKET-DRAFT-kpno-telluric-line-selection.md`. Both look like internal working notes rather than external references, so I did not add rows — your call whether the bibliography should carry them.

## Context

<issue id="d17f8f5c-2c6f-40fb-aed0-f71600f2a9e6" label="RYA-759" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-759/fe-near-uv-synthesis-validate-the-valdturbospectrum-conversion-bsyn" /> landed near-UV Fe I 1D-LTE = 7.487 +/- 0.120 (n=40, 3000-3780 A) and DIAGNOSED the dominant error: line-to-line scatter **0.354 dex**, correlating with nothing measurable (wavelength, chi2r, continuum, depth, EP, log gf all |r| <= 0.21), best/worst fit quartiles differ only 0.08 dex -- so it is NOT fit quality, it is **per-line gf error**. So this is the single biggest lever on the near-UV number. It is the **BLUEWARD twin of** <issue id="dc477121-9a04-424f-819e-4c8a6d3523df" label="RYA-379" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-379/build-extend-canonical-gfcsv-rya-355-guard-past-9199-a-to-cover-the" /> (which extends canonical_gf REDWARD past 9199). Consumes <issue id="19c9a25e-065e-4550-9f83-ba8e5b8fc622" label="RYA-381" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-381/intake-assemble-new-non-optical-vald-extractions-solar-uvred-opticalir" />'s UV VALD intake.

**Parallel to, not overlapping,** <issue id="9d9a3162-0988-4dcd-8744-4164bd358948" label="RYA-799" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-799/investigate-build-grade-or-honestly-bound-the-271-pass-fe-i-ir-lines" /> (which Ryan is starting now): 799 GRADES existing IR lines (6910-9199) with Ruffoni-2014/Belmonte-2017/NIST/GES; THIS extends + adjudicates a NEW band (3000-3780) with UV-appropriate sources. Different band, different sources -- no collision.

## Spec

1. Extend `canonical_gf.csv` (+ the <issue id="4ff86822-9ee8-47d1-9ea8-665c1c5f296d" label="RYA-355" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-355/build-data-stewardship-invariant-check-ci-fail-loudly-on-any-canonical" /> blue-edge guard) blueward of 3780.04 A down to 3000 A, covering the near-UV Fe I pool (759's 40 lines + the full-band candidates).
2. Adjudicate per-line gf against UV-appropriate primary sources: NIST-ASD, GES flags, and **Peterson & Kurucz 2022 (PK-III/PK21)** -- currently SHELVED as a candidate Fe I line-ID resource in <issue id="d7bb9041-77e5-4d2f-bef8-49e5cb3b0689" label="RYA-779" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-779/docs-record-peterson-and-kurucz-2022-apjs-260-28-pk-iiipk21-as-a" />; un-shelve and evaluate it as the blueward gf/line-ID source. Confirm whether Ruffoni-2014/Belmonte-2017 reach blueward (likely IR-only) and record.
3. Attach grade-or-systematic per line (the <issue id="ef9283c3-ba34-467b-93cd-7362e18014fa" label="RYA-711" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-711/traceability-our-line-grade-collides-with-nists-letters-is-circular" /> MQ-grade vocabulary) so the near-UV lines carry defensible gf provenance instead of flat VALD3 scatter.
4. Re-derive the near-UV Fe I product with the adjudicated gf and report the scatter change (0.354 dex is the target to shrink; 3000-3300 A, MAD 0.755, is the worst sub-band).

## Do NOT

* Do NOT tune to the optical or to Asplund (<issue id="68caa0a1-dd50-4c03-8386-a6c7ab48d24b" label="RYA-161" href="https://linear.app/ryans-adventure-zone/issue/RYA-161/science-solar-astrophysical-log-gf-calibration-blue-edge-cut" /> firewall) -- adjudicate against primary gf sources only.

## End-of-Session

Extended canonical_gf blueward to 3000 A, per-line gf grade/systematic for the near-UV band, the re-derived near-UV Fe I product with its new scatter, the PK22 evaluation verdict, branch + SHA. Do NOT merge.

RYA-822: canonical_gf reaches 3000 Å — and grading the near-UV gf changes nothing, because the scatter is the Kurucz floor

comments.body:
CORRECTION (Ryan pushback, 2026-08-15): I claimed the near-UV has "no lab gf to lean on." WRONG -- verified against the literature. Substantial primary lab gf DOES exist in 3000-3780 A:

- **Belmonte, Pickering, Ruffoni, Den Hartog, Lawler et al. 2017** (A&A; arXiv:1710.07571): experimental Fe I log gf spanning **213-1033 nm (2130-10330 A)** -- covers the ENTIRE near-UV band. 120 values from 15 odd-parity levels, many <=0.05 dex.
- **Den Hartog et al. 2014** (ApJS 215, 23): 203 Fe I lines, high-lying even-parity levels.
- **O'Brian et al. 1991** + **NIST ASD** (Kramida et al.): the classic broad Fe I lab set, grades C+ (<=0.12 dex).

So the RYA-759 0.354-dex near-UV scatter is NOT because lab gf don't exist -- it is because canonical_gf.csv does not INGEST them below 3780. This is an UN-INGESTED band, not an ungraded one.

REFRAMED DELIVERABLE: 822 is no longer "extend + flag most SCALE-MISMATCH." It is: extend canonical_gf blueward by **INGESTING the real near-UV lab gf** -- Belmonte 2017 first (it spans the whole band), then O'Brian 1991 / Den Hartog 2014 / NIST ASD -- GRADE the pool against them, and re-derive. Expect the 0.354 scatter to drop substantially, not just get annotated. The near-UV joins the lab-gf sub-pool story (RYA-824), NOT the hopeless-ungraded story.

Still applies: GF- vocabulary (799), positivity guard (825), do NOT tune to optical/Asplund (161). SCALE-MISMATCH stays only for lines where a lab value genuinely does not exist. This ticket just got more valuable -- it can tighten the near-UV bar, not merely label it. Count the actually-gradeable fraction as a deliverable.

## Done — PR #268, branch `ryandamienschmitt/rya-822-nearuv-gf`, tip `d98d05e`. **NOT merged.**

Your inline comment was right on every count, and the payoff test says so.

### The payoff test is a NULL

| | A(Fe I) | scatter | n |
|---|---|---|---|
| VALD as delivered | 7.487 | 0.354 | 40 |
| NIST-adjudicated canonical gf | **7.488** | **0.355** | 40 |

### 🔴 Because the scatter IS the Kurucz floor — measured twice, independently

- Per-line gf source recovered from VALD's **4th physical line** (our built list had flattened it to a uniform `'VALD3'`): **84.3% `gf:K14`, 15.7% no gf tag, ZERO primary lab.**
- Grading the pool through 799's scale: **84.4% `systematic:K07`.**

### 🔴 The actionable finding — your point 3, quantified

> **61 near-UV Fe I lines have a primary laboratory gf. Our list was measured on that value for 6.**
> The other **55 are SCALE-MISMATCH**, |Δ| median 0.092, max 2.961 dex.

799: 36-of-271, 2 used, in the IR. Same shape one band bluer. Re-inverting the 55 is a **pool rebuild, not a grading job** — same conclusion 799 reached; wants its own ticket under RYA-161/398.

### Your three consequences, each honoured

1. **SCALE-MISMATCH reused, not reinvented** — 55 lines. And note the near-UV case differs from 799's in one way worth recording: the synthesis resolves *through* `canonical_gf`, so for adjudicated lines the value and the grade travel together — no fabricated pedigree there.
2. **GF- vocabulary, not MQ-.** Single-sourced through `pipeline/gf_grades.py`. One addition, `GF-NIST`, living in that module with the rest.
3. **Bounded count of real lab gf: six.** Exactly the "honest deliverable" you predicted.

### ⚠️ GF-NIST is deliberately NOT GF-LAB

NIST Fe I here is largely a **compilation** (RYA-760: `FMW` *is* NIST, VALD copies it), so agreement proves no transcription error, not independence. **`is_graded` left unchanged** (still primary-lab only) so this cannot silently restate 799's headline; `GF-NIST` gets its own `has_cited_sigma`.

| grade | n | % |
|---|---|---|
| `systematic:K07` | 3609 | 84.4 |
| `GF-NIST` | 604 | 14.1 |
| `SCALE-MISMATCH` | 55 | 1.3 |
| `GF-LAB` | 6 | 0.1 |

**610 lines now carry a citable per-line σ** — median 0.0414 dex vs the blanket 0.20 (4.8× tighter).

### 🔴 NIST ASD is NOT blocked — this also closes 799's owed item 2

Bisected: server-side fault confined to the **`unit`** parameter. `astroquery.nist` works and returns the `TP`/`Line` refs curl never gave. **`wavelength_type` defaults to `'vacuum'` and our lists are air** (~0.95 Å at 3400 Å) — caught by an offset scan peaking at −1.00 Å, harmless meanwhile only because the matcher also demands EP. Commented on 799 separately.

### Positivity guard adopted

On the VALD parse and on every emitted σ, per your last paragraph.

### ⚠️ Two corrections to my own earlier claims here

1. "Ruffoni/Den Hartog have zero lines below 3780 Å" — true of the **partial** VizieR extracts in `primary_gf/`, **false of the sources**: 799's table spans 2132–11316 Å with **105 Fe I below 3780** (Belmonte2017 70, DenHartog 31, Ruffoni 4).
2. I nearly reported "0 orphans in 3000–3780" off a list **capped at 20**. Real confirmation instead: the guard now treats that window as covered, so an orphan there is **untracked and fails** — stewardship 38 tracked, **0 untracked**.

### Other deliverables

- `canonical_gf.csv` **145,886 → 167,165**, blue edge **3780.038 → 3000.003 Å**, via `cluster_physical_lines` (rounding-based grouping produced rows the resolver couldn't find — caught loudly).
- **PK21: evaluated, NOT adopted as gf.** Table 3 Note 2 makes `log(gf)₀ = log(gf)+dgf` a reference fit — the RYA-161 violation RYA-779 ratified. Its **line IDs** are the value: **~465 of 860** absent from our list (chance-corrected).
- **Stewardship guard fixed** — attribution was direction-blind, sending a 1150 Å line to "past 9199 Å".
- ⚠️ **Scope wider than specified**: `apply_to_synth_array` resolves every species (died on Cr II), so the table had to cover the band, not one element.

Suite **1737 passed / 0 failed**, path gate 0, register **v76**.

INLINE (RYA-799 result, 2026-08-14) -- read before continuing. 799 just proved the Fe line pool's log_gf is **100% Kurucz K14, IR AND optical alike** (un-flattening the VALD3 provenance recovered the source; only 2/271 IR lines were actually measured on a primary lab value). Expect the SAME here: the near-UV pool is almost certainly Kurucz-floored, and the 0.354 scatter IS that floor, worse blueward.

Three consequences for THIS ticket:

1. **Expect SCALE-MISMATCH, not graded recovery.** 799 found canonical_gf carries lab references the POOL DID NOT USE (pool vs canonical log_gf disagree up to 0.96 dex). Attaching those references' accuracy to a Kurucz-derived abundance FABRICATES a pedigree -- graded-looking, ungraded in fact. 799 invented a third state, SCALE-MISMATCH (same bar + flag) for exactly this. Reuse it; do NOT report "graded" off canonical_gf refs the near-UV pool wasn't measured on.

2. **Use the GF- grade vocabulary 799 established, NOT MQ-.** A gf grade is a claim about the atomic datum, not our measurement quality -- 799 keeps GF-/systematic disjoint from MQ- and NIST letters with a test. Single-source through 799's GF- scale.

3. **The near-UV likely has even fewer primary lab gf than the IR** (poorly measured in the lab). So 822's honest deliverable is probably: extend canonical_gf blueward + SCALE-MISMATCH-flag most lines + a bounded count of any with a real lab gf. The actual error lever (re-measuring on primary lab gf) is the separate re-pool ticket.

Adopt 799's permanent **positivity guard** on any UV lab-gf table you parse: a mis-parsed fixed-width table put log gf into the uncertainty column and produced a -2.62 dex sigma that a not-null check waved through; only positivity caught it.

comments.body:
RYA-946's 2026-08-30 ratified definitions are now the binding grading contract for this intake:

- **Codex Grade**: primary-laboratory gf and measured Solar feature depth <= 0.60. Depth below 0.05 is reported separately as below observability, so the operational observable Codex pool is 0.05–0.60.
- **Deep Grade**: the same primary-laboratory gf requirement, with feature depth > 0.60; route to synthesis rather than EW inversion.
- **Asplund Grade**: an orthogonal AGSS21/source-paper reference-line membership axis. It does not imply Codex or Deep grade.
- **Consistent**: parked future evaluated-provenance tier (including the still-open exact NIST threshold); it must not be merged into Codex/Deep.

Feature depth is the maximum component within 0.05 Å in the measured Solar spectrum, matching the Fe treatment. This explicitly supersedes earlier RYA-946 wording that admitted NIST into the active graded pool.

Initial AGSS21 lineage trace is concrete: §2.3 points atomic C/N/O to Amarsi et al. 2019/2020/2018a and the 879-line molecular analysis to Amarsi et al. 2021. AGSS21 reports 39 C2 Swan, 51 CH Δv=1, 7 CH A–X, 28 CO Δv=1, 52 CO Δv=2, 13 NH Δv=0, 15 NH Δv=1, 59 CN 0–0, 463 CN Δv≥1, 84 OH Δv=0, 50 OH Δv=1, and 15 OH Δv=2 transitions. These counts are the extraction completeness checks for the all-band molecular intake. Atomic counts called out are 14 C I plus [C I] 872.7 nm, five N I, and the O indicators [O I] 557.7/630.0/636.4 nm and O I 615.8/777/844.7/926.9 nm.

Source acquisition continues here while final molecular canonicalization remains sequenced behind RYA-1130.
